### **27.1 BasicDataType**

function BasicDataType: string  
  
Returns the basic data type of the term as defined in the database.  
  
Example:  
 function a\_Test: boolean;  
 var  
 oTerm: Object;  
 begin  
 oTerm := application.getterm('procent');  
 message(oTerm.basicdatatype);  
 end;  

### **27.2 DataType**

function DataType: string;  
  
Returns the data type of the term as defined in the Application.  
  
Example:  
 function a\_Test: boolean;  
 var  
 oTerm: Object;  
 begin  
 oTerm := application.getterm('procent');  
 message(oTerm.datatype);  
 end;  

### **27.3 Decimals**

function Decimals:integer  
  
Number of decimals for term. If not definined then -1.  

### **27.4 Header**

function Header:String  
  
Header for current language.  

### **27.5 Length**

function Length:integer  
  
Term length if defined else -1.
  
  

### **27.6 Mask**

function Mask:String  
  
Input format for term.  

### **27.7 MaxChar**

function MaxChar:String  
  
Max number of inputchars, if no such property then length is returned.
If no length property then -1 is returned.  

### **27.8 Prompt**

function Prompt:String  
  
Prompt for current language.  

28 TimeZones
------------

The TimeZones object has methods for retrieving dates/times and converting dates/times between different time zones. The object is retrieved from the Application object.  
  
Example:  
...  
var  
 oTimeZones: Object;
begin  
 oTimeZones := Application.TimeZones;
end;  

### **28.1 ConvertDate**

function ConvertDate( iFromTimeZoneCode: Integer; liDate: Longint; liTime: Longint; iToTimeZoneCode: Integer): Longint;  
  
Converts the specified date to another time zone. Returns the converted date or -1 if the conversion failed.  
  
Note that this function is not implemented in any Jeeves client.  

### **28.2 ConvertDateTime**

function ConvertDateTime( oDateTime: Object; iToTimeZoneCode: Integer): Boolean;  
  
Converts the specified DateTime object to another time zone. Returns True if the conversion succeded otherwise False.  
  
Example:  
...  
var  
 oTimeZones: Object;  
 oDateTime: Object;  
 sMsg: string;
begin  
 oTimeZones := Application.TimeZones;  
 oDateTime := oTimeZones.GetUTCDateTime;  
  
// convert current date/time to Eastern time  
 if( oTimeZones.ConvertDateTime( oDateTime, 35 ) ) then begin  
 sMsg := 'The date and time in time zone 35 (' + oTimeZones.GetName( 35 );  
 sMsg := sMsg + ') is ' + oDateTime.Format( 'yyyy-mm-dd hh:nn:ss' );  
 end  
 else begin  
 sMsg := 'Date and time conversion failed';  
 end;  
  
Message( sMsg );
end;  

### **28.3 ConvertTime**

function ConvertTime( iFromTimeZoneCode: Integer; liDate: Longint; liTime: Longint; iToTimeZoneCode: Integer): Longint;  
  
Converts the specified time to another time zone. Returns the converted time or -1 if the conversion failed.  
  
Note that this function is yet to be implemented in any Jeeves client.  

### **28.4 GetClientCode**

function GetClientCode: Integer;  
  
Returns the time zone code for the Jeeves client.  
  
\* Code >= 0 - The time zone code specified for the client.  
\* Code = -1 - No time zone code was specified the client.  

### **28.5 GetClientLocalDate**

function GetClientLocalDate: Longint;  
  
Returns the current date for the client's local time zone.  

### **28.6 GetClientLocalDateTime**

function GetClientLocalDateTime: Object;  
  
Returns the current date and time as a DateTime object for the client's local time zone.  
  
Example:  
...  
var  
 oTimeZones: Object;  
 oDateTime: Object;  
 sMsg: string;  
 CRLF: string;  
 iTZCode: Integer;
begin  
 CRLF := Chr( 13 ) + Chr( 10 );  
 oTimeZones := Application.TimeZones;  
 oDateTime := oTimeZones.GetClientLocalDateTime;  
 iTZCode := oDateTime.GetTimeZoneCode; // we could also use oTimeZones.GetClientCode  
  
if( iTZCode <> -1 ) then begin  
 sMsg := 'Client local date and time information ' + CRLF + CRLF;  
 sMsg := sMsg + 'Time zone: ' + iTZCode + ' (' + oTimeZones.GetName( iTZCode ) + ')' + CRLF;  
 sMsg := sMsg + 'Current date/time: ' + oDateTime.Format( 'yyyy-mm-dd hh:nn:ss' );  
 end  
 else begin  
 sMsg := 'There is no time zone information set for this client';  
 end;  
  
Message( sMsg );
end;  

### **28.7 GetClientLocalTime**

function GetClientLocalTime: Longint;  
  
Returns the current time for the client's local time zone.  

### **28.8 GetName**

function GetName( iTimeZoneCode: Integer): string;  
  
Returns the name of the specified time zone.  
  
Example:  
...  
var  
 oTimeZones: Object;  
 iTZCode: Integer;
begin  
 oTimeZones := Application.TimeZones;  
 iTZCode := oTimeZones.GetClientCode;  
 Message( 'The client time zone is ' + iTZCode + ' - ' + oTimeZones.GetName( iTZCode );
end;  

### **28.9 GetUTCDate**

function GetUTCDate: Longint;  
  
Returns the current UTC date.  

### **28.10 GetUTCDateTime**

function GetUTCDateTime: Object;  
  
Returns the current UTC date/time as a DateTime object.  
  
Example:  
...  
var  
 oTimeZones: Object;  
 oDateTime: Object;
begin  
 oTimeZones := Application.TimeZones;  
 oDateTime := oTimeZones.GetUTCDateTime;  
  
// the date/time will be formatted like 'Wednesday, October 14, 2009, 16:30 PM'  
 Message( 'Current UTC date/time is ' + oDateTime.Format( 'dddd, mmmm d, yyyy, hh:mm AM/PM' ) );
end;  

### **28.11 GetUTCTime**

function GetUTCTime: Longint;  
  
Returns the current UTC time.  

29 Transaction
--------------

### **29.1 SetTopSearch**

Procedure SetTopSearch (Integer);  
  
Limits the search results to the specified number of hits.  
  
Example:   
  
- To limit the search results to the top 10 hits: sub.SetTopSearch(10);   
 - To reset to any number of results: sub.SetTopSearch(0);
  

### **29.2 Commit**

Function commit: boolean;  
  
Completes the action initiated on the transaction object. All client logic will be run when initiating the action. Returns true if successful, otherwise false.  

### **29.3 GetPrimaryKey**

Function GetPrimaryKey : Object  
  
Gets a key object containing all fields that are part of the primary key for the record created in the transaction by the Commit function. Returns a key object which has following functions:  
 - Count - returns number of fields in the primary key  
 - GetTable(i:integer); - returns the table of the primary key field i  
 - GetField(i:integer); - returns the field of the primary key field i  
 - GetValue(i:integer); - returns the value of the primary key field i  

### **29.4 SetValue**

Function SetValue(sTable:string; sField:string; sValue:string)  
  
Sets the value of a field in the current record loaded in the transaction object.  

### **29.5 StartInsert**

Procedure StartInsert;  
  
Initiates an insert operation on the current transaction object.  

### **29.6 StartDelete**

Procedure StartDelete;  
  
Initiates a delete operation on the current transaction object.  
 - StartDelete = current loaded record  
 - StartDelete(iPosition:integer) = record in list (0=first, 1=second)  

### **29.7 StartUpdate**

Procedure StartUpdate;  
  
Initiates an update operation on the current transaction object.  
 - StartUpdate = current loaded record  
 - StartUpdate(iPosition:integer) = record in list (0=first, 1=second)  

### **29.8 StartSearch**

Procedure StartSearch;  
  
Starts a search.  

### **29.9 RefreshList**

Procedure RefreshList;  
  
Reloads list of current transaction objects.   

### **29.10 ShowForm**

function testShowForm: boolean;  
  
Function to navigate to the form window of the row in the embedded list.  

### **29.11 AddCondition**

function AddCondition(sTable: string; sField: string; sOperator: string; sValue : string): boolean;  
  
Adds the condition passed in parameters.  
  
sTable - Table name - can be empty - in which case the function will use focused field  
 sField - Field name - can be empty - in which case the function will use focused field  
  
If the field is not found for the above combination it returns False.  
  
sValue - Value for the condition  
  
sOperator can be text as below, which will be used to create the condition text.  
 '='  
 '<='  
 '>='  
 '<>'  
 '!='  
 '<'  
 '>'  
 'between'  
 'like'  
 'not like'  
  
Returns True when the condition is added successfully.  

30 XmlParser
------------

The XMLParser object has methods for parsing and creating XML files. Are used in user functions for Tacton, Astro and EDI integration.
Example:  
...  
var  
 oXMLParser: Object;
begin  
 oXMLParser:= Application.GetXmlParser;
end;  

### **30.1 CreateXmlFromJvsdbFormat**

function CreateXmlFromJvsdbFormat(sSqlExpression, rowSeparator, columnSeparator):string;  
  
Generates the XML from the result of SQL mentioned in sSqlExpression.  
  
function kn\_createxmldoc: boolean;
var  
 oParser : Object;  
 rowSeparator, columnSeparator, sXmlString, sSqlExpression : string;  
  
begin   
 rowSeparator:='';  
 columnSeparator:='$';  
   
 oParser :=Application.GetXmlParser;  
  
sSqlExpression := 'EXECUTE Jeeves\_Get\_XmlOut\_Mapping
1,
"Order",
0,
0' ;   
  
sXmlString := oParser.GetXmlOutMapping(sSqlExpression, rowSeparator, columnSeparator);  
 Message(sXmlString);  
  
sSqlExpression := '
EXECUTE Jeeves\_Create\_XmlOut\_Result1
@nForetagKod = 1,
@nTranId = -99,
@sModelId = "Order",
@nIntegrationId = 10,
@sVersion = "1.0",
@nRuntime = 0, --0=From mapping,1=Runtime
@sKey1 = '', --Key1-.. value from mapping or runtime queue
@sKey2 = '',
@sKey3 = '',
@sKey4 = '',
@sKey5 = '',
@sKey6 = '',
@sKey7 = '',
@sKey8 = '',
@sKey9 = '',
@sKey10 = '',
@nDebug = 0  
  
';   
 sXmlString := oParser.CreateXmlFromJvsdbFormat(sSqlExpression, rowSeparator, columnSeparator);  
 Message(sXmlString);  
 oParser.Close;
kn\_createxmldoc:=TRUE;
end;  

### **30.2 GetXmlOutMapping**

function GetXmlOutMapping(sSqlExpression, rowSeparator, columnSeparator):string  
  
Parses the data in sSqlExpression using rowSeparator and columnSeparator and builds the internal mapping structure used in the call to CreateXmlFromJvsdbFormat.  
  
function kn\_createxmldoc: boolean;
var  
 oParser : Object;  
 rowSeparator, columnSeparator, sXmlString, sSqlExpression : string;  
  
begin   
 rowSeparator:='';  
 columnSeparator:='$';  
   
 oParser :=Application.GetXmlParser;  
  
sSqlExpression := 'EXECUTE Jeeves\_Get\_XmlOut\_Mapping
1,
"Order",
0,
0' ;   
  
sXmlString := oParser.GetXmlOutMapping(sSqlExpression, rowSeparator, columnSeparator);  
 Message(sXmlString);  
  
sSqlExpression := '
EXECUTE Jeeves\_Create\_XmlOut\_Result1
@nForetagKod = 1,
@nTranId = -99,
@sModelId = "Order",
@nIntegrationId = 10,
@sVersion = "1.0",
@nRuntime = 0, --0=From mapping,1=Runtime
@sKey1 = '', --Key1-.. value from mapping or runtime queue
@sKey2 = '',
@sKey3 = '',
@sKey4 = '',
@sKey5 = '',
@sKey6 = '',
@sKey7 = '',
@sKey8 = '',
@sKey9 = '',
@sKey10 = '',
@nDebug = 0  
  
';  
 sXmlString := oParser.CreateXmlFromJvsdbFormat(sSqlExpression, rowSeparator, columnSeparator);  
 Message(sXmlString);  
 oParser.Close;
kn\_createxmldoc:=TRUE;
end;  

### **30.3 Open**

procedure Open(xmlFileToParse : string; type:integer);  
  
Set text string to parse and type of file to parse (0 for XML and 1 for XSD).  
  
function openParser: boolean;
var  
 oParser : Object;
begin  
 oParser :=Application.GetXmlParser;  
 oParser.Open(xmlmapping.XmlDoc, '0');  
 oParser.Close;
end;
  

### **30.4 SetParserMode**

procedure SetParserMode(iMode:integer);  
  
Sets type of mode when parsing file. 0 for Tacton xml with special attribute format and 1 for Astro/EDI and other xml types.  
  
Example:  
oParser.SetParserMode(0);  

### **30.5 SetRootInXml**

procedure SetRootInXml(sRoot:string);  
  
Sets root in xml to be used when parsing xml file.   
  
Example:  
oParser.setrootinxml('session/view/report/part');

1 .Net Integration
------------------

### **1.1 LoadAssembly**

  
*function LoadAssembly(s : string) : object;*  
  
From version: 3.0  
  
Load an .Net assembly as an object, so it is accessible from JML. The assembly is loaded by the client.  
  

### **1.2 LoadServerAssembly**

  
*function LoadServerAssembly(s : string) : object;*  
  
From version: 3.0  
  
Load an .Net assembly as an object, so it is accessible from JML. The assembly is loaded by the client.  
  

2 Blob functions
----------------

### **2.1 BlobGetLength**

  
*function BlobGetLength( table, field : string ) : integer;*  
  
Returns the number of characters in the Edit field (Blob) whose table and term names match the string argument.  
  
Example: i1 := BlobGetLength('oh', 'edit');  
  

### **2.2 BlobSet**

  
*procedure BlobSet( BlobTable, BlobField, SourceTable, SourceField: string );*  
  
Replaces the content in the Edit field (Blob), which matches the BlobTable and BlobField parameters with the content in the field, which matches the SourceTable and SourceField parameters.  
  
Example: BlobSet(oh, edit, oh, Editext);  
  

### **2.3 BlobCat**

  
*procedure BlobCat( BlobTable, BlobField, SourceTable, SourceField : string );*  
  
Links together the content in the Edit field (Blob) which matches the BlobTable and BlobField parameters with the content in the field which matches the SourceTable and SourceField parameters, e.g.: BlobCat('oh', 'edit', 'oh', 'Editext');  
  

3 Check-off lists
-----------------

### **3.1 ListSaved**

  
*function ListSaved(ctxt : object) : boolean;*  
  
Returns True if all records in cached table (e.g. right-hand window for matching list) for specified window contexts have been written to the database. The function is only relevant when used together with copying between several embedded window contexts. Ctxt is identified with the command UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list).  
  

### **3.2 Parent**

  
*function Parent(ctxt : object) : object;*  
  
Returns a pointer to Parent for a specified window context. NOTE. Do NOT use this function for a program's main window context!  
  

### **3.3 Sibling**

  
*function Sibling(ctxt : object;idx : integer) : object;*  
  
Returns a pointer to Sibling, in this context means 'child', (according to index 0,1,2..) to a specified window context. If a specified window context does not exist, 0 is returned.  
  

### **3.4 MarkAll**

  
*procedure MarkAll(ctxt : object);*  
  
Sets the 'Selected' flag on all records in a cached table for specified window contexts. The function is only relevant when used together with copying between several embedded window contexts.  
  

### **3.5 SaveList**

  
*function SaveList(ctxt : object) : boolean;*  
  
Saves all rows that have not yet been saved in a cached table for specified window contexts. Returns True if the operation is successful. The function is only relevant when used together with copying between several embedded window contexts.  
  

### **3.6 ListLoaded**

  
*function ListLoaded(ctxt : object) : boolean;*  
  
Returns True if the list in a specified window context contains data. Ctxt is identified with the command UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list).  
  

### **3.7 ClearCache**

  
*procedure ClearCache(ctxt : object);*  
  
Empties the list in the window that the whole number ctxt points to, which is retrieved with the command Sibling or UpperCtxt.  
  
Example:  
  
1. Emptying of list to current form.  
  
function clear\_list  
var  

wcont : object;

begin  

wcont := upperctxt(-1);

clearcache(wcont);

end;  
  
2. Emptying of embedded list with highlight on overlying form.  
  
function clear\_embedded\_list  
var  

wcont : object;

begin  

wcont := upperctxt(-1);

wcont:=sibling(wcont,0);

clearcache(wcont);

end;  
  
  

### **3.8 UpperCtxt**

  
*function UpperCtxt(ctxt: object): object;*  
  
Returns a pointer to the window context 'above' what is specified in the Ctxt parameter.  
  
If ctxt is 0, the pointer to an overlying context to the active window context is returned.  
  
If ctxt is -1, the active window context is returned.  
  
If ctxt is a window context at the top level, zero is returned.  
  

### **3.9 IsTransToCache**

  
*function IsTransToCache:boolean;*  
  
Returns True if current Update/Insert statement updates the cache (e.g. right-hand window in a matching list) or False if it updates the table.  
  

4 Comm ports
------------

### **4.1 CommPortOpen**

  
*function CommPortOpen(sPort: string; iBaud: integer; sParity: string; iData, iStop: integer): integer;*  
  
Opens a communication port for reading and writing of data.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- in] sPort (Port to open, e.g. 'COM1:)- [in] iBaud (Baud rate, e.g. 9600)- [in] sParity (Parity (N = none, E = Even or O = Odd))- [in] iData (Data bits, e.g. 8)- [in] iStop (Stop bits (0 ==> 1, 1 ==> 1.5 or 2 ==> 2))

  
**Return values:**

- >= 0 'Port handle' to use with other port management functions.- < 0 Operation failed.

  

### **4.2 CommPortRead**

  
*function CommPortRead(iHandle: integer; sBuffer: string; iCount: integer): integer;*  
  
Reads a character buffer from a communication port.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] iHandle ('Port handle')- [in] sBuffer (Read buffer)- [in] iCount (Number of characters in the buffer that will be read from the port)

  
**Return values:**

- = 0 Number of characters that the operation succeeded in reading from the port.- < 0 Operation failed.

  

### **4.3 CommPortWrite**

  
*function CommPortWrite(iHandle: integer; sBuffer: string; iCount: integer): integer;*  
  
Writes a character buffer to a communication port.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] iHandle ('Port handle')- [in] sBuffer (Buffer to write to the port)- [in] iCount (Number of characters in the buffer that will be written to the port)

  
**Result:**

- = 0 Number of characters that the operation succeeded in writing to the port.- < 0 Operation failed.

  

### **4.4 CommPortClose**

  
*function CommPortClose(iHandle: integer): integer;*  
  
Closes previously opened communication port.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] iHandle ('Port handle')

  
**Return values:**

- < 0 Operation failed.

  

5 Currencies
------------

### **5.1 MoneyAsString**

  
*function MoneyAsString( Language : integer; Value : money ) : string;*  
  
Returns the value of the Money type, which is specified in the Value parameter, and displays it as a string in the language specified by the language code.  
  
Example:   
  
function MoneyAsString: boolean;  
begin  
Message( MoneyAsString(999, oh.ordsum ) );  
end;  
  

### **5.2 IsViewingEuro**

  
*function IsViewingEuro:boolean;*  
  
Returns True if base currency is displayed in Euro.  
  
Example:  
  
function IsViewingEuro: boolean;  
begin  
Message(IsViewingEuro);  
end;  
  

6 Date/time
-----------

### **6.1 DateToString**

  
*function DateToString(aDate : longint) : string;*  
  
Returns a date string in the format 'yymmdd'. The argument is translated to number of days from 01/01/1600.  
  
Example: str1 := DateToString(oh.ordberlevdat);  
  

### **6.2 TimeToString**

  
*function TimeToString(aTime : longint) : string;*  
  
Returns a time string in the format 'hh.mm'. The argument is interpreted as the number of seconds from midnight.  
  
Example: str1 := TimeToString(22000);  
  

### **6.3 StringToDate**

  
*function StringToDate(s : string) : longint;*  
  
Converts a string in the format 'YYMMDD' to Long integer which represents the number of days since 01/01/1600. In the event of an error -1 is returned.  
  
Example: longInt1 := StringToDate('020407');  
  

### **6.4 StringToTime**

  
*function StringToTime(s : string) : longint;*  
  
Converts the string 's' in the format 'HH:MM' or 'HH.MM' to Long integer which represents the number of seconds since midnight. In the event of error -1 is returned.  
  
Example: longInt1 := StringToTime('14:47');  
  

### **6.5 Today**

  
*function Today : longint;*  
  
Returns a Long integer which represent the number of days from 01/01/1600 to today's date according to the computer's internal clock.  
  
Example: longInt1 := Today;  
  

### **6.6 Now**

  
*function Now : longint;*  
  
Returns a whole number which represents the number of seconds from midnight to the current time according to the computer's internal clock.  
  
Example:   
  
function now: boolean;  
var  
lNow: longint;  
begin  
lNow := Now;  
Message(Now);  
end;  
  

### **6.7 DateToMaskedString**

  
*function DateToMaskedString( Format : string; Date : longint ) : string;*  
  
Returns the date as a string in the format specified by the Format parameter.   
If Format is blank (''), a default date format is used.  
If Format is blank (''), and there is no default date format, 'yymmdd' is assumed as a format.  
  
Example:  
  
function Test:boolean;  
where  
s : string;  
begin  
s:=DateToMaskedString( 'yyyy-mm-dd', today);  
Messages( s );  
Test:=true;  
end;  
  

### **6.8 MaskedStringToDate**

  
*function MaskedStringToDate( Format, Date : string ) : longint;*  
  
The string that contains the date is translated according to the specified format and is converted to Longint.  
  
If Format is blank (''), a default date format is used.  
If Format is blank (''), and there is no default date format, 'yymmdd' is assumed as a format.  
  
Example:  
function MaskedStringToDate: boolean;  
var  
lDate: longint;  
begin  
lDate := MaskedStringToDate('dd-MM-yyyy', '26-10-2017');  
Message( lDate );  
end;  
  

7 DDE commands
--------------

Recommendation: To make the macro future safe, variables that receive the macro objects (e.g. Application object, Form object, List object, etc.) must be of Object datatype.  

### **7.1 DDEConnect**

  
*function DDEConnect(AServer, ATopic: string): object;*  
  
Links to a DDE server application.   
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sServer (The server application you want to link to)- [in] sTopic (The "function" you want to activate)

  
The parameter 'AServer' must be specified as 'Jeeves\_' + database name, i.e. if the Jeeves application you want to link to is run against the 'test' database, the parameter should be specified as 'jeeves\_test' .  
  
'ATopic' should be 'none' or a string consisting of ';. The latter only functions if the specified context is active in Jeeves.  
  
**Return values:**

- 0 = No link available- >0 = Link identifier used for continued DDE calls.

  
**Example:**

- where hConv: object;

  
hConv := DDEConnect('jeeves\_test', 'none')   
Or  
hConv := DDEConnect('jeeves\_test', 'order1;orderh')  
  

### **7.2 DDEDisconnect**

  
*procedure DDEDisconnect(hConv: longint);*  
  
Disconnects and closes communication with another DDE server application.  
  
The argument hConv = 'handle\* which is returned for earlier calls to function DDEConnect.  
  
Example: DDEDisconnect(hConv);  
  

### **7.3 DDEExecute**

  
*function DDEExecute(hConv: longint; Cmd: string): boolean;*  
  
Sends a command string to the server application for the relevant DDE link. The string format must conform to the Microsoft standard for this. See separate list of available DDE commands in Jeeves DDE server.  
  
Example:  
Assume that we have a DDE link, which is identified by the variable hConv, and that 'cmd' is a command that the DDE server we are connected to understands. The following row executes 'cmd' in the DDE server:  
  
DDEExecute(hConv, [cmd] );  
  

### **7.4 DDERequest**

  
*function DDERequest(hConv: longint; Item: string; var rs: string): boolean;*  
  
Requests specific data from the server application in the current DDE link. See separate list of available DDE functions in Jeeves DDE server.  
  
Example:  
Assume that we have a DDE link, which is identified by the variable 'hConv', and that 'req' is a request that the DDE server we are connected to understands. The return value ends in the variable res.  
  
DDERequest(hConv, req, res );  
  

### **7.5 DDEPoke**

  
*function DDEPoke(hConv: longint; Item: string; Data: string): boolean;*  
  
  

### **7.6 DDEExecuteEx**

  
*function DDEExecuteEx(hConv: longint; Cmd: string): boolean;*  
  
Expanded function of DDEExecute. The difference is that this function calls the DDE server asynchronously, that it does not wait for a response and therefore can never cause a DDE timeout.  
  
  

### **7.7 DDERequestEx**

  
*function DDERequestEx(hConv: longint; Item: string; liTimeOut: longint; var rs: string): boolean;*  
  
Expanded function of DDERequest. By expressing timeout in milliseconds you can control the time that the function will wait for a response from the DDE server. If you enter 0 (zero) the call is performed asynchronously.  
  
Example:  
According to the example under DDERequest, with 'req', which is a request that the DDE server understands. The result ends in the variable res.  
  
DDERequestEx(hConv, req, 3000, res);  
  

### **7.8 PostInternDDEExecute**

  
*procedure PostInternDDEExecute( cmd : string );*  
  
Sends a DDE Execute command to an incoming DDE queue to be executed when the macro has finished.  
  

8 e-Mail
--------

### **8.1 SaveMail**

  
*function SaveMail(sPathName, sFileNamePrefix: string; var sFileNameExt: string): integer;*  
  
Saves opened email in Outlook or opened document in Notes. If Notes is used and if the operation is successful, the total number of selected documents is returned.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sPathName (Full path)- [in] sFileNamePrefix (Filename without file extension)- [in/out] sFileNameExt (File extension. If set to msg (only Outlook) or txt, a file is created in the specified format. All other extensions produce txt files)

  
Return values (from 133):  
SUCCESS >= 0 (total number of documents to save)  
ERROR\_UNKNOWN = -1000  
ERROR\_MAIL\_PROGRAM\_NOT\_ACTIVE = -1001  
ERROR\_MAIL\_ATTACHMENT\_NOT\_FOUND = -1002  
ERROR\_MAIL\_COMPONENT\_MISSING = -1003  
ERROR\_DOCUMENT\_NOT\_FOUND = -1004  
ERROR\_MAIL\_NO\_DOCUMENT\_SELECTED = -1007  
  
Return values (older versions):  
0 - Success  
1000 - ERROR\_UNKNOWN  
1001 - ERROR\_NO\_ACTIVE\_INSPECTOR  
  

### **8.2 SaveMailAttachment**

  
*function SaveMailAttachment(iIndex: integer; sPathName, sFileNamePrefix: string; var sFileNameExt: string): integer;*  
  
Saves attachments according to specified index in opened email in Outlook or in the first of selected documents in Notes.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in) iIndex (Index for email attachments (counted from 1))- [in] sPathName (Full path)- [in] sFileNamePrefix (Filename without extension)- [out] sFileNameExt (File extension)

  
Return values (from version 133):  
SUCCESS = 0  
ERROR\_UNKNOWN = -1000  
ERROR\_MAIL\_PROGRAM\_NOT\_ACTIVE = -1001  
ERROR\_MAIL\_ATTACHMENT\_NOT\_FOUND = -1002  
ERROR\_MAIL\_COMPONENT\_MISSING = -1003  
ERROR\_DOCUMENT\_NOT\_FOUND = -1004  
ERROR\_MAIL\_NO\_DOCUMENT\_SELECTED = -1007  
  
Return values (older versions):  
0 - Success  
1000 - ERROR\_UNKNOWN  
1001 - ERROR\_NO\_ACTIVE\_INSPECTOR  
1002 - ERROR\_INVALID\_INDEX  
  

### **8.3 GetMailAttachmentInfo**

  
*function GetMailAttachmentInfo(iIndex: integer; var sFileName: string; var sFileExt: string): integer;*  
  
Retrieves information on attachments according to specified index in opened email in Outlook or in the first of selected documents in Notes. If this is successful, the total number of attachments is returned.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] iIndex (Index for email attachments (counted from 1))- [out] sFileName (Filename)- [out] sFileExt (File extension)

  
Return values (from version 133)  
SUCCESS >= 0 (total number of attachments)  
ERROR\_UNKNOWN = -1000  
ERROR\_MAIL\_PROGRAM\_NOT\_ACTIVE = -1001  
ERROR\_MAIL\_ATTACHMENT\_NOT\_FOUND = -1002  
ERROR\_MAIL\_COMPONENT\_MISSING = -1003  
ERROR\_DOCUMENT\_NOT\_FOUND = -1004  
ERROR\_MAIL\_NO\_DOCUMENT\_SELECTED = -1007  
  
Return values (earlier versions):  
0 - Success  
1000 - ERROR\_UNKNOWN  
1001 - ERROR\_NO\_ACTIVE\_INSPECTOR  
1002 - ERROR\_INVALID\_INDEX  
  

### **8.4 SendMail**

  
*function SendMail(sTo : string; sCC : string; sBCC : string; sSubject : string; sMessage : string; sAttachments : string; sOptions : string; bDialog: Boolean): Integer;*  
  
From version: 32 v126  
  
Beginning with version 1.5 onwards, the limit of 16t is removed in terms of the number of recipients and attached files. However, the underlying system may have other limits.   
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sTo (Recipient. If more than 1 separate with ; )- in] sTo (Copies to recipient. If more than 1 separate with ; )- [in] sBCC (Blind copies to recipient. If more than 1 separate with ; )- [in] sSubject (Header)- [in] sMessage (Message)- [in] sAttachments (Files to be attached. If more than 1 separate with ; )- [in] sOptions (Reserved for future use)- [in] sDialog (From. version 32.133 can be set to TRUE which means that installed email client starts. Set to FALSE for older versions of Jeeves clients)

  
Result:  
SUCCESS = 0  
ERROR\_UNKNOWN = -1000  
ERROR\_MAIL\_COMPONENT\_MISSING = -1003  
ERROR\_MAIL\_SENDING\_FAILED = -1005  
ERROR\_MAIL\_LOGOUT\_FAILED = -1006  
  
Example:  
iResult := SendMail(SMTP:support@jeeves.se,'', '','Hi, we have a problem...','c:\temp\log.txt','',FALSE)  
  
  
  

9 External reports
------------------

### **9.1 WriteCrystalFileInfo**

  
*procedure WriteCrystalFileInfo;*  
  
  
This kernel function has no effect anymore since other crystal functions already handle this.  
  
Updates the file u2ljvs.dat in the CRYSTAL directory so that the Crystal Reports reports that use Jeeves translation macros are linked to the right instance of Jeeves.  
  

### **9.2 CrystalPrint**

  
*function CrystalPrint(sReportFile: string; bPreview: boolean; sPrinterName: string; iNrOfCopies: integer; sWhere: string; bReplaceWhere, bProcReport: boolean; sProcParams: string; bWait: boolean):integer;*  
  
Prints or previews a Crystal Reports report.  
  
Parameter description:  
\* [in] sReportFile (Full path and name for report file)  
\* [in] bPreview (True means Preview, False means Print on a printer)  
\* [in] sPrinterName (Ignored if bPreview is True)   

DIALOG (Show print dialog)

DEFAULT (Use default printer)

\* [in] iNrOfCopies (Number of copies to print (ignored if bPreview is True))  
\* [in] sWhere (Where-clause to add to original Where-clause)  
\* [in] bReplaceWhere (Replaces original Where-clause with the parameter sWhere)  
\* [in] bProcReport (True if report is a procedure-based report)  
\* [in] sProcParams (Procedure parameters, delimited with | (ignored if bProcReport is False))  
\* [in] bWait (If True, print jobs are handled in sequence (normally True))  
  
The function returns negative values when it fails and below are some possible error codes.  
  
ERROR\_UNKNOWN = -1000;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_OPEN        = -4001;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_PRINTER\_SELECT = -4002;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_PRINTER\_SET = -4003;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_SETSELECTIONFORMULA = -4004;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_START = -4005;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_GETSQLQUERY = -4006;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_SETSQLQUERY = -4007;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_WINDOWREDIR = -4008;  
ERROR\_CRYSTAL\_GETSELECTIONFORMULA = -4009;  
  

### **9.3 CrystalExportToHtml**

  
*function CrystalExportToHtml(sReportFile, sHtmlFile, sHtmlDir, sWhere: string; bReplaceWhere, bProcReport: boolean; sProcParams: string; bWait: boolean):integer;*  
  
Exports a Crystal Reports report to an HTML document.  
  
NOT TO BE USED FROM KERNEL 2.0.2 - USE CRYSTALEXPORTTOFILE INSTEAD.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sReportFile (Full path and name for report file)- [in] sHtmlFile (Relative filename for HTML document to create)- [in] sHtmlDir (Directory where HTML document will be created)- [in] sWhere (Where-clause to add to original Where-clause)- [in] bReplaceWhere (Replaces original Where-clause with the parameter sWhere)- [in] bProcReport (True if report is a procedure-based report)- [in] sProcParams (Procedure parameters (ignored if bProcReport is False))- [in] bWait (If True, print jobs are handled in sequence (normally True))

  

### **9.4 CrystalGetLastPrintJob**

  
*function CrystalGetLastPrintJob: integer;*  
  
Returns ID for last print job handled by Crystal Reports print engine. Sequence number starting from 0, which means that no report has been run.  
  
Not supported in Crystal Reports 2008.  
  

### **9.5 CrystalGetLastSqlQuery**

  
*function CrystalGetLastSqlQuery: string;*  
  
Returns SQL clause for the last report run. Note that there is no guarantee that the report printout was successful. The function can be used for troubleshooting in reports where the result was not as intended. With regard to the limited length of macro strings, you should not store the result in a string but instead call the message function Message(CrystalGetLastSqlQuery) directly.  
  

### **9.6 CrystalExportToFile**

  
*function CrystalExportToFile(sReportFile, sExportlFile, sExportDir, sWhere: string; bReplaceWhere, bProcReport: boolean; sProcParams: string; bWait: boolean):integer;*  
  
Exports a Crystal Reports report to a file (pdf,rtf,html).  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sReportFile (Full path and name for report file)- [in] sExportFile( Name for the file, the suffix settle the export type)- [in] sExportDir (Directory where the document will be created)- [in] sWhere (Where-clause to add to original Where-clause)- [in] bReplaceWhere (Replaces original Where-clause with the parameter sWhere)- [in] bProcReport (True if report is a procedure-based report)- [in] sProcParams (Procedure parameters (ignored if bProcReport is False))- [in] bWait (If True, print jobs are handled in sequence (normally True))

  
**Other formats supported include:**

- Word (doc)- xcel (xls),- ext (txt)- Comma separated values (csv)

  
If you use datetime in your where-clause, the CONVERT command can be used to convert it to correct syntax.  
How to use CONVERT:  
  
sWhere := 'olh.ordberlevdat= CONVERT(datetime,'+toSQL(DateToMaskedString('YYYYMMDD',olh.ordberlevdat))+')';  
  
- Space between "=" and "CONVERT".  
- CONVERT needs to be in uppercase.  
- The date should contain a four-digit year.  
  

### **9.7 SSRSPrint**

  
*function SSRSPrint(sReportFile: string; bPreview: boolean; sPrinterName: string; iNrOfCopies: integer; sWhere: string; bProcReport: boolean; sProcParams: string):Boolean;*  
  
Prints or previews an SSRS report.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- in] sReportFile (Report path on reporting services (e.g. SSRSReports/MonthlySalesReport))- [in] bPreview (True means Preview, False means Print on a printer)- [in] sPrinterName (Ignored if bPreview is True)- DIALOG (Show print dialog)- DEFAULT (Use default printer)- [in] iNrOfCopies (Number of copies to print (ignored if bPreview is True))- [in] sWhere (Where-clause to add to original Where-clause)- [in] bProcReport (True if report is a procedure-based report)- [in] sProcParams (Procedure parameters, delimited with & (ignored if bProcReport is False))

  

### **9.8 SSRSExportToFile**

  
*function SSRSExportToFile (sReportFile, sExportlFile, sExportDir, sWhere: string; bProcReport: boolean; sProcParams: string):Boolean;*  
  
Exports an SSRS report to a file (pdf,rtf,html).  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sReportFile (Report path on reporting services (e.g. SSRSReports/MonthlySalesReport))- [in] sExportFile ( Name for the file, the suffix settle the export type)- [in] sExportDir (Directory where the document will be created)- [in] sWhere (Where-clause to add to original Where-clause)- [in] bProcReport (True if report is a procedure-based report)- [in] sProcParams (Procedure parameters, delimited with & (ignored if bProcReport is False))

  
If you use datetime in your where-clause, the CONVERT command can be used to convert it to correct syntax.  
  
How to use CONVERT:  
  
sWhere := 'olh.ordberlevdat= CONVERT(datetime,'+toSQL(DateToMaskedString('YYYYMMDD',olh.ordberlevdat))+')';  
  
- Space between "=" and "CONVERT".  
- CONVERT must be in uppercase.  
- The date must contain a four-digit year.  
  

10 Field management
-------------------

### **10.1 MarkField**

  
*function MarkField(t: string; f: string): boolean;*  
  
Flags a field with a tick in the form so that it is added to the search filter.   
  
Example:  
bSuccess := MarkField('oh', 'ftgnamn');  
  
The command does not set focus in the field (i.e. the cursor is placed there). If this is desired, the command FocusField must be used.  
  
  

### **10.2 RunPostFieldChange**

  
*procedure RunPostFieldChange(t: string; f: string);*  
  
Runs the procedure that is associated with the PostFieldChange event, i.e. forces Jeeves to validate the field Table.field in the current form.  
  
Example: RunPostFieldChange( 'oh', 'ftgnr' );  
  

### **10.3 FocusField**

  
*function FocusField(t: string; f: string): boolean;*  
  
Sets a highlight on the specified field in the form or list, depending on which one is active.   
If the form is active, the field will be marked and will thereby be included in the search term.  
  
Example:  
bSuccess := FocusField('oh','ftgnr');  
  
If no marking is desired (red check) the command FocusFormField must be used.  
If you explicitly want to set focus on the list or form, the command FocusListField or FocusFormField must be used.  
  
  

### **10.4 IsTermVisible**

  
*function IsTermVisible( tname : string ):boolean;*  
  
Returns True if specified term is visible.  
  
Example: ftgnr\_is\_visible := IsTermVisible( 'ftgnr' );  
  

### **10.5 FocusListField**

  
*procedure FocusListField( tblid, id : string );*  
  
Highlights a field in the list. Corresponds to FocusField but applies to the list instead of the form. Changes to the list if the form is in focus.  
  
Example:   
FocusListField('orp', 'artnr');  
  

### **10.6 GetCurrentField**

  
*procedure GetCurrentField(var sTable:string; var sField:string);*  
  
From version: 32 v135  
  
Retrieves table name, field name for the highlighted field in question.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [ut] sTableName (table name)- [ut] sFieldName (name of the field)

  
Example:  
Note that before you run this macro, you should mark the relevant field.  
function GetCurrentField: boolean;  
var  
sTable, sField : string;  
begin  
GetCurrentField := True;  
GetCurrentField( sTable, sField);  
Message('Table is ' + sTable);  
Message('Field is ' + sField);  
end;  
  

### **10.7 SetFieldProperty**

  
*function SetFieldProperty(sTable:string; sField:string; iProperty:integer; sValue:string):Boolean;*  
  
From version: 32 v135  
  
Sets the specified field property to the desired value. This works only in forms, in other words, not in lists. Returns false if it is unsuccessful.   
  
The function (with PROP\_DATA = 1) should be used instead of SendKey to send data to the field.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sTableName (name of table which includes the field)- [in] sFieldName (name of the field)- [in] iProperty (The property to be set)- [in] sValue (The value the property will be given)

  
Note that the font size and font type are not supported in the Desktop client.   
  
Property constants for iProperty:  
PROP\_DATA = 1;  
PROP\_BGCOLOR = 2  
PROP\_FONT = 3  
PROP\_FONTSIZE = 4  
PROP\_FONTCOLOR = 5   
PROP\_ENABLED = 6  
PROP\_PROMPT\_FONTCOLOR = 7  
PROP\_PROMPT\_TEXT = 8  
PROP\_HEADER\_TEXT = 9  
PROP\_READONLY = 10  
PROP\_MASK = 11  
PROP\_VISIBLE = 12  
PROP\_NOTABSTOP = 13  
  
As of version 220b also user defined button properties can be changed (but only enabled and visible).  
To do this set the tablename to 'zsbutton' and fieldname to the siterepository id (only buttons in new site works) for the button.  
  
Example:  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',1,'kalle');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',2,'Silver');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',3,'Impact');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',4,'12');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',5,'GREEN');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',6,'False');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',7,'Red');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',8,'My company prompt');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',9,'My company list header');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',10,'true');  
SetFieldProperty('ar','artvikt',11,'mm2b');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',12,'false');  
SetFieldProperty('fr','ftgnamn',13,'true');  
SetFieldProperty('ar', 'artvolym',11,'mm2"b');  
SetFieldProperty('ar', 'artvolym',11,'mm2"d');  
  
SetFieldProperty('zsbutton','20000',6,'false');  
  
Possible colors:  
Red        
Green        
Blue  
Black        
Yellow        
Gray        
White        
Silver  
or in Hexadecimal   
exampel red = #FF0000  
  
  

### **10.8 FocusFormField**

  
*function FocusFormField(t: string; f: string): boolean;*  
  
From version: 32 v135 Beta1b  
  
Sets a highlight on the specified field in the form. Changing to a form occurs in cases where focus is on a field in the list.  
The field will not be included in the search term which FocusField makes.   
The function is not applicable for changing focus from an embedded list to its form.  
  
Example:  
bSuccess := FocusFormField('oh','ftgnr');  
  
If you need to specify an exact field (the same field i.e. table.columnname can exists many times in a form window) you can use the unique id instead.  
  
Example:  
bSuccess := FocusFormField('\_\_id','50');  
  

### **10.9 RunFieldChangeAsClient**

  
*procedure RunFieldChangeAsClient( t: string; f: string );*  
  
From version: v203  
  
Run the procedure that is associated with the PostFieldChange-event, that is forcing Jeeves to validate the field Table.field in the current form.   
Furthermore, executes the code (procedure) related to the PostSelectRelated-event.  
  
Example: RunFieldChangeAsClient( 'oh', 'ftgnr' );

### **11.1 SqlOutputToFile**

  
*function test\_SqlOutputToFile: boolean;*  
  
This function returns the SqlOutputToFile object.   
  
var  
O : object;  
path : string;  
begin  
O := Application.SqlOutputToFile;  
if O = 0 then begin  
Message( 'Application.SqlOutputToFile is not implemented in current kernel version' );  
Exit;  
end;  
  
//Message( O.members ); // show all members to object SqlOutputToFile  
  
path := 'D:\Jeeves'; //Any valid directory path within single quotes or variables and fields  
  
if copy ( path , length ( path ) , 1 ) <> '\' then  
path := path + '\';  
  
path := path + 'FixFiles\Nisse1.txt';  
//Message( path );  
  
O.AsSingleColumn( TRUE ); // default = TRUE  
O.AddNewLineAtEndOfRow( TRUE ); // default = TRUE  
O.PrintErrMsg( FALSE ); // default = TRUE if false then check Status and Message  
O.FileName( path );  
O.MaxColLength(10);  
O.SqlStmt( 'select cast(12345 as varchar(20));' );  
O.Execute;  
if O.getStatus <> 0 then begin  
message( 'Error executing Application.SqlOutputToFile.'  
+ NewLine + 'Status = ' + O.GetStatus  
+ NewLine + 'Error message = ' + O.GetMessage  
);  
end else begin  
message( 'OK'  
+ NewLine + 'GetNumberOfRows = ' + O.GetNumberOfRows  
+ NewLine + 'GetNumberOfChars = ' + O.GetNumberOfChars  
+ NewLine + 'GetMaxRowLength = ' + O.GetMaxRowLength  
);  
end;  
end;

### **11.12 FileCompress**

  
*function FileCompress(sFileName:string; sFiles:string ;bRecurse, bStripPath:boolean;sOption:string):integer;*  
  
From version: 32 v126  
  
Creates a compressed file in Zip format and if the file already exists puts the specified files into it.   
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sFileName (Name of the compressed file (should end with .zip))- [in] sFiles (Files to be compressed. Multiple files can be separated with the | character, but this is not possible with recurse option set )- [in] bRecurse (If set to TRUE the content in all subfolders will be added to the file)- [in] bStripPath (If set to TRUE the file will not contain a folder structure)- [in] sOption (reserved for future use)

  
Return codes:  
No of files added  
ERROR\_UNKNOWN = -1000;  
ERROR\_FAILED\_TO\_OPEN\_SOURCE\_FILE = -1106  
  
Example:  
c:\temp\Word.doc " Compresses the file Word.doc.  
c:\temp\\*.\* " Compresses all files in the temp folder.   
c:\temp\\*.doc " Compresses all doc files in the temp folder.  
c:\temp\file1.doc|c:\temp\file2.doc compresses file1 and file2  
  
Example of using this macro with a file structure as follows:  
  
C:\temp\PDF1.pdf  
C :\temp\PDF2.pdf  
...  
C:\temp\Word1.docx  
C:\temp\Word2.docx  
...  
C:\temp\F1\Test1.txt  
C:\temp\F1\Test2.txt  
...  
C:\temp\F2\Test3.txt  
C:\temp\F2\Test4.txt  
  
1. To create a compressed file test.zip which includes all the files and subfolders without retaining the folder structure:  
begin  
FileCompress('C:\temp\output\test.zip','C:\temp\\*.\*',TRUE,TRUE,'');  
end;  
  
2. To create a compressed file test.zip which includes all the files and subfolders retaining the folder structure:  
begin  
FileCompress('C:\temp\output\test.zip','C:\temp\\*.\*',TRUE,FALSE,'');  
end;  
  
3. To create a compressed file test.zip including files and sub folders retaining the folder structure:  
begin  
FileCompress('C:\temp\output\test.zip','C:\temp\\*.\*',FALSE,FALSE,'');  
end;  
Note that though the parameter bRecurse is FALSE, a compressed file test.zip including files and sub folders is created (as \*.\* is used in the sFiles parameter indicating that everything under the temp folder should be included). The parameter bRecurse will have effect only if sFiles has a file extension type.

*function FileDialog(iType:integer; sTitle, sInitialDir, sFilter:string; bMultiSelect, bFileMustExist:boolean; var sFileName:string) : Boolean;*

### **11.16 FileUnCompress**

  
*function FileUnCompress(sFile:string; sFilesToExtract:string; sTargetPath:string; bOverridepath, bOverwrite, bClientSide:Boolean):integer;*  
  
From version: v2.3  
  
Extract files from a compressed file in Zip format.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sFile (Name of the compressed file (should end with .zip))- [in] sFilesToExtract (\*.\* for all files or name of a specific file)- [in] sTargetPath (Where to extract the file, if only one file a name can be specifed)- [in] bOverridepath (The internal folder structure in the zip will not be used)- [in] bOverwrite (If the file exist in target, should it be overwritten)- [in] bClientSide (if false the operation is done at the server side)

  
If bClientSide = False the path must be defined in the Applicable server paths (spth) program.  
  
Example:  
You can provide input for the sFilesToExtract parameter as follows:  
\*.\* - Extracts all the files in a compressed file  
\*.txt - Extracts all the files of a specific file type in a compressed file  
abc.\* - Extracts all the files of a specific name but different file type in a compressed file  
Word.doc - Extracts the specific file Word.doc in a compressed file  
  
Example of using this macro to extract files from a compressed file without maintaining its original file structure:  
  
Test.zip has following files compressed in it:  
- test.zip -> testfolder -> abc.txt  
- test.zip -> testfolder -> def.txt  
- test.zip -> testfolder -> pdf1.pdf  
- test.zip -> testfolder -> pdf2.pdf  
  
begin  
FileUnCompress('C:\temp\input\test.zip','\*.\*','C:\temp\Output',TRUE,TRUE,TRUE);  
end;  
  
- This command uncompresses the test.zip file and extracts all the files(\*.\*) into the Output folder. The folder structure of the compressed file will not be retained while uncompressing as the bOverridepath parameter is True.   
- If any existing files with the same name as the files to be extracted are available in the Output folder, they will be overwritten as the bOverwrite parameter is True.  
- The extraction of the files occurs on the Client side as the bClientSide parameter is True.

Possible values, ascii (default), utf16, utf8

12 Form functions
-----------------

### **12.1 InsertFlag**

  
*function InsertFlag(ctxt : object) : boolean;*  
  
Returns current setting for whether SQL Insert operations are allowed in the specified window context. Ctxt is identified with command UpperCtxt or Sibling(embedded lists). The setting is normally True, but False can be set in PreInsert and InInsert to cancel the Insert operation.  
  

### **12.2 UpdateFlag**

  
*function UpdateFlag(ctxt : object) : boolean;*  
  
Returns current setting for whether SQL Update operations are allowed in the specified window context. The setting is normally True, but False can be set in PreUpdate and InUpdate to cancel the Update operation.  
  

### **12.3 DeleteFlag**

  
*function DeleteFlag(ctxt : object) : boolean;*  
  
Returns current setting for whether SQL Delete operations are allowed in the specified window context (identified with command UpperCtxt). The setting is normally True, but False can be set in PreDelete and InDelete to cancel the Delete operation.  
  
Example:  
wcont:=UpperCtxt(-1);  
message(deleteflag(wcont));  
  

### **12.4 SetInsertFlag**

  
*procedure SetInsertFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
(Re)does the setting for whether SQL Insert operations are allowed in the specified window context. The setting is normally True, but False can be set in PreInsert and InInsert to cancel the Insert operation.  
  

### **12.5 SetUpdateFlag**

  
*procedure SetUpdateFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
(Re)does the setting for whether SQL Update operations are allowed in the specified window context. The setting is normally True, but False can be set in PreUpdate and InUpdate to cancel the Update operation. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  

### **12.6 SetDeleteFlag**

  
*procedure SetDeleteFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
Sets setting for whether SQL Delete operations are allowed in the specified window context. The setting is normally True, but False can be set in PreDelete and InDelete to cancel the Delete operation. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  

### **12.7 VTabFlag**

  
*procedure VTabFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
Returns a Boolean value in the Flg parameter. The value specifies whether entry of detail records will be initiated automatically after the main record is saved.  
  
Return values:  
True = Initiate entry of detail records automatically  
False = Do NOT initiate entry of detail records automatically  
  
This macro function should not be used as it has been deferred pending modifications.  
  

### **12.8 SetVTabFlag**

  
*procedure SetVTabFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
(Re)does the setting for whether you will come to the first embedded list after new record entry in a specified window context. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  

### **12.9 DetailLoadFlag**

  
*procedure DetailLoadFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
Set to True if all information will be loaded for every loading of a record to a form. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  
This macro function should not be used as it has been deferred pending modifications.  
  

### **12.10 SetDetailLoadFlag**

  
*procedure SetDetailLoadFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
False for current window context (Ctxt) means that data will NOT be loaded into a detail window when a record is retrieved to the main window. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  

### **12.11 total**

  
*function total(field: string): real;*  
  
Retrieves the value from a total field. The field must be in the active window context. The Field parameter will contain the name for the total term in the total window.  
Can only return values from fields that is a user function or a part of the programs maintable.  
  
Example:   
MyReal := total('OrdSumBas')  
  

### **12.12 TermExists**

  
*function TermExists(t: string; f: string): boolean;*  
  
Returns True if the term to which 't' (= table) and 'f' (= field) point is in the current view.  
  
Example: bool1 := TermExists('fr', 'ftgnamn');  
  

### **12.13 SetRefreshFlag**

  
*procedure SetRefreshFlag(ctxt: object);*  
  
After a call to SetRefreshFlag(ctxt), data will be reloaded ('refresh') in a specified window context the next time the window is opened. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  

### **12.14 SearchMode**

  
*function SearchMode(ctxt: object): boolean;*  
  
Returns TRUE if the current window context (ctxt) is in search mode, i.e. not in edit or new entry mode. Ctxt 0 = current context.  
  

### **12.15 SetCopyNextFlag**

  
*procedure SetCopyNextFlag(ctxt : object;flg : boolean);*  
  
False means that the next record from the source window context will NOT be copied when the new entry command is given. Ctxt is obtained with the commands UpperCtxt or Sibling (embedded list). See example for ClearCache.  
  

### **12.16 DeleteRecord**

  
*function DeleteRecord(ask\_okcancel: boolean): boolean;*  
  
Attempts to delete current record. The user is asked to confirm the deletion if ask\_okcancel is True.  
  
Example: DeleteRecord(TRUE);  
  

### **12.17 GetCondStr**

  
*function GetCondStr: string;*  
  
Returns the SQL term that will be used for printing the report. If the JINI parameter FormCondInReport = N the SQL term for the current record will be returned. If FormCondInReport = Y, the current search filter, i.e. what is shown when using the button See terms, is returned.   
Example: str1 := GetCondStr;  
  
Note that this function has been deprecated and should not be used after kernel 3.0.0. Use instead some of the following alternative depending on what you want to achive.  
  
//return where statment for what the user has marked for search in the client  
oForm := Application.GetCurrentForm  
oForm.GetSearchCondStr  
  
or  
  
//return the where statment for the current record in the form  
oForm := Application.GetCurrentForm  
oForm.GetCondStr  
  
or  
  
//return the where statement that has been used the to get the list records  
oList := Application.GetCurrentList  
oList.GetCondStr  
  
  

### **12.18 GetMode**

  
*function GetMode: integer;*  
  
Returns the current window context's mode.  
  
Return values:  
0 = View mode  
1 = Entry mode (new entry)  
2 = Change mode  
  
Example: int1 := GetMode;  
  

### **12.19 EditToCombo**

  
*function EditToCombo( TableId, TermId , SqlStmt, Table2id, Term2ID : string ):boolean;*  
  
Converts an Edit field in a form into a drop-down list (combo box).  
  
Parameters:  
\* [in] TableId & TermId (ID of the Edit field to convert to a drop-down list)  
\* [in] SqlStmt (Select-clause to get content for drop-down list)  
\* [in] Table2Id (Name of the source table)   
\* [in] Term2Id (Reserved for future use)  
  
Return value: True if the operation is successful, otherwise False.  
  
Example:  
EditToCombo( 'oh', 'ftgnr', 'select distinct ftgnamn, ftgnr from fr', 'fr', );  
  
Please note that the drop-down list cannot contain duplicates, i.e. the select-clause must result in only single strings.  
  

### **12.20 LoadEditCombo**

  
*function LoadEditCombo( TableId, TermId, SqlStmt : string ):boolean;*  
  
Reloads the content in an Edit field that has been converted into a dropdown list (combobox) using the EditToCombo function.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] TableId (Table ID for the Edit-combo field that will be reloaded)- [in] TermId (Field ID for the Edit-combo field that will be reloaded)- [in] SqlStmt (Select-clause for the content in the Edit-combo field)

  
Example:   
LoadEditCombo('oh','ftgnr','select distinct ftgnamn,ftgnr from fr');  
  
Return values: True if reloading is successful, otherwise False.

Example: EditCopy('fr','ftgnamn');

Clicks the button associated with the table and field. Use '\_\_func' as table name to click on a "User function" button.  
  
It is also possible to "click" on customer own added buttons by using the button ID and an empty table name.  
The button ID is shown on the button when using Ctr+Alt+F12.  
  
Example:  
PressButton('oh','edit');      (\* Opens Edit-button in the order entry \*)  
PressButton('\_\_func','Push\_Button\_OhTfnNr');       (\* Press on function button Tfn/Fax in the order entry \*)

13 Insight

14 Macro execution
------------------

### **14.1 ExecProgram**

  
*function ExecProgram(Program, Params: string): boolean;*  
  
Starts another Windows application from within Jeeves. Note: In the Desktop client this functionality requires that you have High security level. (Elevated is not sufficient.) You acheive this by installing Jeeves Silverlight helper on the client computers.  
  
Example: ExecProgram('H:\WINWORD\WINWORD', '/mMyMacro');  
  
The path to the application must be specified in the format 8.3 characters. If a file pointer is specified in the first argument (Program) and the second argument is blank (Params), the file is opened with the program that Windows associates with the file extension.  
  

### **14.2 PostRunMacro**

  
*function PostRunMacro( MacroName:string ):boolean;*  
  
Runs a named macro after the current (calling) macro has finished.  
  
Example: bool1 := PostRunMacro('theNameOfaMacro');  
  
DoOnIdle should be used instead. In some environments, the following construction can be used:  
  
if GetJMLPlattform=32 then  
DoOnIdle( 'Macro2', true )  
else  
PostRunMacro( 'Macro2' );  
  
Note that when linking to an event that requires a return value, the called macro will be executed only after the event has been implemented.   
  

### **14.3 Exit**

  
*procedure Exit;*  
  
Closes a macro.  
  

### **14.4 ExecProgramEx**

  
*function ExecProgramEx(Program, Params: string; nCmdShow:boolean):boolean;*  
  
Starts another Windows application (see ExecProgram).  
  
Example: ExecProgramEx('H:\WINWORD\WINWORD', '/mMyMacro',0)  
  
The parameter nCmdShow can have the following values:  
  
SW\_SHOWNORMAL       1  
SW\_NORMAL       1  
SW\_SHOWMINIMIZED 2  
SW\_SHOWMAXIMIZED 3  
SW\_MAXIMIZE       3  
SW\_SHOWNOACTIVATE 4  
SW\_SHOW             5  
SW\_MINIMIZE       6  
SW\_SHOWMINNOACTIVE 7  
SW\_SHOWNA       8  
SW\_RESTORE 9  
  

### **14.5 ProcessMessages**

  
*function ProcessMessages:boolean;*  
  
Processes the message queue. This makes it possible to have several PostMenuCommand in the same macro. Note that processing depends on the Windows message queue, which means that the command may not function in all modes. This has no function in the Classic client.  
  
Example:  
  
function t1:boolean;  
var  
b : boolean;  
begin  
PostMenuCommand( 'add' );  
b:=ProcessMessages;  
  
while b do  
begin  
b:=ProcessMessages;  
end;  
  
oh.Ftgnr:='1030';  
RunPostFieldChange( 'oh', 'ftgnr' );  
PostMenuCommand( 'save' );  
  
while ProcessMessages do;  
  
FocusListField( 'orp','artnr' );  
SendKey( '123456' );  
  
while ProcessMessages do;  
  
PostMenuCommand( 'save' );  
  
while ProcessMessages do;  
  
  
end;  
  

### **14.6 PostRunUFU**

  
*procedure PostRunUFU( UFName : string );*  
  
Runs a named 'User function', found in Appl.ufu, after the current (calling) macro has finished. When linking to an event that requires a return value, the called User function will be executed only after the event has been implemented.   
  
User functions can also be executed directly in a macro by specifying the function name.  
  
  

### **14.7 Sleep**

  
*procedure Sleep(iMilliseconds: longint);*  
  
Stops the program batch for a specified number of milliseconds.  
  

### **14.8 DoOnIdle**

  
*procedure DoOnIdle( sMacroName : string; bMacroUFU : boolean );*  
  
From version: 32 v135 Beta1d  
  
DoOnIdle stores a macro run until everything else has been processed. The macro will be executed just before the server engages in the mode to be able to receive new commands from the user.  
  
Should be used instead of PostRunMacro.  
  
The bMacroUFU parameter specifies if it is a user function or a macro is to be run.  
bMacroUFU=true provides a macro.  
bMacroUFU=false runs a user function.  
  
Note that when linking to an event that requires a return value, the called macro will be executed only after the event as been implemented.  
  

### **14.9 MacroExists**

  
*function MacroExists( sName : string ) : boolean;*  
  
From version: 32 v1.50  
  
Search for a macro with the name specified by the input parameter. If the macro exists, the function TRUE returns, otherwise FALSE.  
  

### **14.10 FunctionExists**

  
*function FunctionExists( sName : string ) : boolean;*  
  
From version: 33 v1.50  
  
Search for a function with the name specified by the input parameter. If the function exists, the function TRUE returns, otherwise FALSE.  
  

### **14.11 KernelFunctionExists**

  
*function KernelFunctionExists( sName : string ) : boolean;*  
  
From version: 33 v1.50  
  
Search for a kernel function with the name specified by the input parameter. If the kernel function exists, the function TRUE returns, otherwise FALSE.  
  

15 Mathematical functions
-------------------------

### **15.1 ln**

  
*function ln(x:real):real;*  
  
Returns natural logarithm of x.  
  
Example: real1 := Ln(4.7);  
  

### **15.2 exp**

  
*function exp(x:real):real;*  
  
Returns exponent e raised to x ( ex ).  
  
Example: real1 := Exp(2.5);  
  

### **15.3 sqrt**

  
*function sqrt(x:real):real;*  
  
Returns the square root of the argument (Floating point or Integer).  
  
Example: real1 := Sqrt(9);  
  

### **15.4 abs**

  
*function abs(x:real):real;*  
  
Returns the absolute value of x, i.e. -x if the value for x is negative, otherwise x.  
  
Argument: optional numeric value, e.g.: r1 := Abs(-3.4);  
  

### **15.5 Check10**

  
*function Check10( str:string ):boolean;*  
  
Returns True if the string's last digit is a valid check digit according to module 10, calculated based on the other digits in the string.  
  
Example: Check10('5556444');  
  

### **15.6 Check11**

  
*function Check11( str:string ):boolean;*  
  
Returns True if the string's last digit is a valid check digit according to module 11, calculated based on the other digits in the string.  
  
Example: Check11('5556444');  
  

### **15.7 GenCheck10**

  
*function GenCheck10( Digits : string ):string;*  
  
Returns the check digit according to module 10 for the digits in the argument.  
  
Example: str1 := GenCheck10('555333');  
  

### **15.8 GenCheck11**

  
*function GenCheck11( Digits : string ):string;*  
  
Returns the check digit according to module 11 for the digits in the argument.  
  
Example: str1 := GenCheck11('555333');  
  

### **15.9 Power**

  
*function Power(base, exponent:real):real;*  
  
Calculates the base raised to the exponent:  
  
Power(10,2)=100   
  
...because   
  
10^2=100  
  

### **15.10 NumberToWords**

  
*procedure NumberToWords( iLang:integer; value:real; sCurr:string;var sWholePart:string; var sDecimalPart:string);*  
  
From version: v203  
  
Function to translate a number into words and replace MoneyAsString. This functionality is implemented for English, Polish and Lettish only. If it needs to be used for any other language, it must be ordered via your Jeeves representative.  
  
If sDecimalPart is set to / the decimal is represented as a fraction with the base 100 (e.g. 31/100).  
If sDecimalPart is set to # the decimal is represented unmodified.  
If the specified currency code is Polish (PLN) or Lettish (LVL) the name of the currency will be added to the returned string.  
  
This is only introduced in the original language. Otherwise the currency code has to added explicitly to the texts when the commando is executed ( see example 3 below).  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] iLang (Language code to which the number will be translated - currently only English, Polish or Lettish)- [in] Value (Number to be translated)- [in] sCurr (Currency code, if a processed currency is specified then the name of currency will be added in the return string)- [out] sWholePart (The whole number part will be translated into words)- [out] sDecimalPart (The decimal number part will be translated into words)

  
Example 1:  
NumberToWords(19,100.50,'',sWhole,sDecimal);  
  
Message(sWhole + ' ' + sDecimal);  
(sWhole = Viens simts)  
(sDecimal = Piecdesmit)  
  
Example 2:  
NumberToWords(19,100.50,'LVL',sWhole,sDecimal);  
  
Message(sWhole + ' ' + sDecimal);  
(sWhole = Viens simts lati)  
(sDecimal = Piecdesmit santmi)  
  
Example 3:  
NumberToWords(19,100.50,'LVL',sWhole,sDecimal);  
sWhole := sWhole + 'lat';  
sDecimal := sDecimal + ' santims';  
  
Message(sWhole + ' ' + sDecimal);  
(sWhole = Viens simts lat)  
(sDecimal = Piecdesmit santims)

19 Program management
---------------------

### **19.1 PostMenuCommand**

  
*procedure PostMenuCommand(s : string);*  
  
Activates one of the commands on the menu after the macro has finished.  
The following value can be set in parameter s:  
add  
clear  
delete  
refresh  
expand  
up  
ctrlz  
left  
right  
modify  
save  
search  
print  
copyemb  
firstpost  
nextpost  
previouspost  
lastpost  
loadpost  
  
Example:   
PostMenuCommand('refresh');  
  
You can also send menu codes in the same way as with ClickMenuItem (for more information see MenuCommand and see separate chapter with list of menu codes). We recommended that you use PostMenuCommand rather than ClickMenuItem, because the name is better when the command is being executed and this command will be further developed whereas ClickMenuItem will only be maintained for reverse compatibility.  
  
Example:   
PostMenuCommand(909);      (\* Performs refresh \*)  
  
Note that there may be a delay before the command is actually executed. The command is normally executed after the calling macro is finished. If you want the command to be executed directly, use the MenuCommand function.  
  

### **19.2 SendKey**

  
*procedure SendKey( characters : string );*  
  
Sends the string to the highlighted window.  
  
Example:  
SendKey ('hi'); (\*sends the text 'hi' to the active field or the Edit field.\*)  
  
The following special characters are available:  
~K = Alt + K  
^K = Ctrl + K  
etc.  
  
In the Classic client, the function should be replaced by:  
SetFieldProprty:      To send text into a field. Current field is identified with GetFieldProperty.  
MenuCommand:      To execute a menu alternative (which also includes practically all shortcuts).  
  
Example of placing text in current field where the cursor is located and then searching.  
GetCurrentField(sTable,sField);  
SendKey('%');  
LoadFromGui(sTable,sField);  
PostMenuCommand('search');  
  
Note that this macro function is not implemented for the Desktop client.

Saves data from an active field to paste in using PreformDrop.  
  
Example: StoreAsdragItem;  
  

### **19.4 PreformDrop**

  
*procedure PreformDrop;*

Example: PreformDrop;

### **19.12 GetMenuItem**

  
*function GetMenuItem( Parent, id : longint; text : string ) : longint;*  
  
Retrieves a menu handle/ID for a menu option on Jeeves menu bar. GetMenuItem can retrieve a menu ID for Crystal Reports (only by using the description) & Print to screen.  
  
All positions are calculated from 0 and the line that divides the menus into different sections can also be calculated.  
  
If Parent is set to 0, this means the main menu.  
  
An option can be retrieved using its position or its description.  
- If ID lies in the interval 0 and 100, the option is retrieved using its position, the Text parameter is ignored.  
  
- Otherwise the option is retrieved using its text string.  
  
Note that this macro function is not implemented for the Desktop client.  
  
Example:  
  
Item:=GetMenuItem(0,5,'');  
  
Returns the handle for the Tools menu on the menu bar.  
  
If Item is then used as Parent:  
  
Item:=GetMenuItem(Item,0,'');  
  
...an ID is returned for the 'Edit terms' menu option on the Tools menu.  
  
The value can be used together with the function MenuCommand to activate the menu option.  
  

### **19.13 ClickMenuItem**

  
*function ClickMenuItem( item :integer ):boolean;*  
  
Activates a menu option on the Jeeves menu, clicks on a button or sends a key press after the macro has been completed.   
The required option is specified with item parameter. There are fixed codes for Jeeves standard options (see separate list). Own menu options are returned with the GetMenuItem function.  
  
Note:  
From version 1.5, this macro function has become obsolete and should not be used. Instead, either MenuCommand or PostMenuCommand should be used depending on when the command is to be executed.  
  

### **19.14 SetGlobalData**

  
*function SetGlobalData( ID : string; Data : string ):boolean;*  
  
Can contain an optional data type and associates the value with the ID string. This can then be used with the GetGlobalData function.  
  
function test1:boolean;  
var  
s : string;  
i : integer;  
l : longint;  
begin  
s:='Hi';  
i:=1;  
l:=2;  
SetGlobalData( 'S1', s );  
SetGlobalData( 'S2', i );  
SetGlobalData( 'S3', l );  
  
s:='';  
i:=0;  
l:=0;  
GetGlobalData( 'S1', s );  
GetGlobalData( 'S2', i );  
GetGlobalData( 'S3', l );  
  
Message( s );  
Message( i );  
Message( l );  
end;  
  
  

### **19.15 GetGlobalData**

  
*function GetGlobalData( ID : string; Data: string ):boolean;*  
  
Retrieves the value associated with the ID string previously specified in the SetGlobalData function.  
  
function test1:boolean;  
var  
s : string;  
i : integer;  
l : longint;  
begin  
s:='Hi';  
i:=1;  
l:=2;  
SetGlobalData( 'S1', s );  
SetGlobalData( 'S2', i );  
SetGlobalData( 'S3', l );  
  
s:='';  
i:=0;  
l:=0;  
GetGlobalData( 'S1', s );  
GetGlobalData( 'S2', i );  
GetGlobalData( 'S3', l );  
  
  
Message( s );  
Message( i );  
Message( l );  
end;
