Prints selected report with specified template in existing program.   
This command is obsolete and should not be used starting with version 2.0 of the kernel.   
Instead, the RunReport command or the Report object should be used since they have the same functionality.  
  
**Parameters:**

- [in] sRepName (Name of the report).- [in] sTemplateName (Name of the template).- [in] sCondition (Search terms for the printout).- [in] sParams (Parameters, separated with the | symbol, for reports with data dialog boxes).

  
sParams does not work with multigetstring functionality.  
  
Example:  
  
Print out a report with template and current list selection.  
s1:= Getcondstr;  
RunReportInPgm('rkp1','Lasse1',s1,'');  
  

### **19.21 MenuCommand**

  
*function MenuCommand(item :longint):boolean;*  
  
From version: 32 v1.50  
  
Activates a menu option on the Jeeves menu or click on a menu button.  
The required option is specified with item parameter.   
There are fixed codes for Jeeves standard options (see separate list in chapter 1007).  
Text argument is listed under PostMenuCommand.   
Own menu options are returned with the GetMenuItem function.  
  
This command is executed directly, which in certain cases does not function as desired, especially if the macro is run in an event. In these cases, PostMenuCommand must be used.  
  
Example:  
MenuCommand(901);  
bpi.lagplats := '111A';  
MenuCommand(902);  
PostMenuCommand('refresh');  
  
  
  

### **19.22 PrimaryKey**

  
*function PrimaryKey (ctxt: object; iType: integer) : string;*  
  
From version: 2.0  
  
Returns the primary key fields values separated by ;. Triggered after loading a record.  
  
Example: message( PrimaryKey( 0, 1) );  
  
Currently, this functionality is not supported on any Jeeves client.  
  

20 SQL functions
----------------

### **20.1 SqlBegin**

  
*procedure SqlBegin(s : string);*  
  
Prepares to execute a specified SQL statement. SqlBegin must be followed by SqlExecute and SqlEnd. Statements that will return values will include SqlBind and SqlFetch.  
  
Example:  
  
Function ex\_sql:Boolean;  
var s1:string;  
  
Begin  
s1:='SELECT FtgNr FROM th where th.ForetagKod='+ToSQL(bh.ForetagKod)+  
'and th.AoNr='+ToSQL(bh.AoNr);  
SqlBegin(s1);  
SqlBind(bh.FtgNr);  
if SqlExecute then  
begin  
while SqlFetch do begin  
(\* DO SOMETHING \*)  
End;  
SqlEnd;  
end  
else  
begin  
SqlEnd;  
JEEVES\_Sql\_Error('ex\_sql',s1);  
end;  
End;  
  

### **20.2 SqlBind**

  
*procedure SqlBind(var x : string);*  
  
Links a program variable to SQL Server data when using SQLFetch.  
  
Kernel versions older than 3.0 can bind to max 255 but in newer versions, the result will be half of the value defined in the MaxBlobSize kernel parameter. For example, if the value in the MaxBlobSize parameter is set to 40000 characters, the fetch limit will be 20000 characters.   
  
It is recommended that you use SQLBindEx function to avoid memory related errors.  
  

### **20.3 SqlExecute**

  
*function SqlExecute : boolean;*  
  
Executes the SQL commands previously specified in a call to SqlBegin.  
  

### **20.4 SqlFetch**

  
*function SqlFetch : boolean;*  
  
Loads the next record from the hit quantity in SQL Server.  
  

### **20.5 SqlEnd**

  
*procedure SqlEnd;*  
  
Releases buffers and links used for communication with SQL Server.  
  

### **20.6 toSQL**

  
*function toSQL(x: string): string;*  
  
Formats the string according to correct SQL syntax.  
  
Example: str1 := ToSql('oh.ftgnr');  
  

### **20.7 SQLGetString**

  
*function SQLGetString( s : string ) : string;*  
  
From version: 32 v1.50  
  
Simplified function for entering a text from the database.  
  
For entering text from the database, the following steps must normally be carried out (see also SqlBegin):  
- SqlBegin(s);  
- SqlBind(x);  
- SqlExecute;  
- SqlFetch ... until FALSE  
- SqlEnd;  
  
With this function, you only need to do:  
- SQLGetString(s);  
  
Note:  
SQLGetString can be carried out even if you have an active SqlBegin, which has not concluded with an SqlEnd;  
SQLGetString is NOT carried out within a transaction (SqlBegin can, for certain macro points, include a transaction).  
SQLGetString only deals with the first column in an SQL set (select col1, col2 from table, only includes the value in col1).  
If you want to enter data from several columns, you can merge these (see the example below).  
If the SQL set involves matches on several rows in the database, then the results are entered from all rows with a new row (chr(13)+chr(10)) between each row.  
The maximum result size for SQLGetString is 160000 characters, which means the fetch limit is 159999 characters.  
  
Example:  
  
function a\_\_sm: boolean;  
where  
s1, sr, sc : string;  
amt : money;  
begin  
s1 := SQLGetString( 'select top 3 ArtNr+space(2)+coalesce(ArtBeskr,space(0))+char(1)+cast(ArtListPris as varchar(30)) from ar where ArtListPris<>0' );  
Message( s1 );  
sr := ExtractString ( s1, chr(13)+chr(10), 1 );  
Message( sr );  
sc := ExtractString ( sr, chr(1), 1 );  
sc := ExtractString ( sr, chr(1), 2 );  
Message( 'Item='+sc+', price='+amt\*1.25 );  
end;  
  
Info: space(2) gives two spaces, space(0) gives an empty string but not NULL, space(-1) gives NULL  
  

### **20.8 SQLGetInteger**

  
*function SQLGetInteger( s : string ) : HugeInt;*  
  
From version: 32 v1.50  
  
Simplified function for entering a whole number value from the database.  
  
For entering text from the database, the following steps must normally be carried out (see also SqlBegin):  
- SqlBegin(s);  
- SqlBind(x);  
- SqlExecute;  
- SqlFetch ... until FALSE  
- SqlEnd;  
  
With this function, you only need to do:  
- SQLGetInteger(s);  
  
Note:  
SQLGetInteger can be carried out even if you have an active SqlBegin, not concluded with an SqlEnd;  
SQLGetInteger is NOT carried out within a transaction (SqlBegin can, for certain macro points, include a transaction).  
SQLGetInteger only deals with the first column in an SQL set (select col1, col2 from table, only includes the value in col1).  
  
  
Example:  
  
function a\_\_sm: boolean;  
where  
L1 : LongInt;  
begin  
L1 := SQLGetInteger( 'select count(\*) from ar where ArtListPris=0' );  
end;  
  

### **20.9 SqlExecuteText**

  
*function SqlExecuteText( s : string ) : boolean;*  
  
From version: 2.0  
  
A simplified function to perform an operation in the database will not return any data.  
If data is returned (from select sets) it is disregarded.  
  
Note:  
SQLExecuteText can be carried out even if you have an active SqlBegin, which has not concluded with an SqlEnd;  
SQLExecuteText is NOT carried out within a transaction (SqlBegin can, for certain macro points, include a transaction).  
  
Example:  
  
function a\_\_sm: boolean;  
where  
b1 : boolean;  
begin  
b1 := SqlExecuteText( 'execute my\_own\_procedure' );  
end;  
  

### **20.10 SqlBeginDirect**

  
*procedure SqlBeginDirect( sSql : string );*  
  
From version: v2.2.1  
  
Prepares to execute a specified SQL statement. SqlBegin must be followed by SqlExecute and SqlEnd. Statements that will return values will include SqlBind and SqlFetch.  
SqlBeginDirect bypasses the TSQL-Conversion if running with a different database than SQLServer  
  
Example:  
  
Function ex\_sql:Boolean;  
var s1:string;  
  
Begin  
s1:='SELECT FtgNr FROM th where th.ForetagKod='+ToSQL(bh.ForetagKod)+  
'and th.AoNr='+ToSQL(bh.AoNr);  
SqlBeginDirect(s1);  
SqlBind(bh.FtgNr);  
if SqlExecute then  
begin  
while SqlFetch do begin  
(\* DO SOMETHING \*)  
End;  
SqlEnd;  
end  
else  
begin  
SqlEnd;  
JEEVES\_Sql\_Error('ex\_sql',s1);  
end;  
End;  
  

### **20.11 SqlBeginTran**

  
*procedure SqlBeginTran;*  
  
From version: v3.0  
  
Starts a transaction in the database.  
  

### **20.12 SqlRollbackTran**

  
*procedure SQLRollbackTran;*  
  
From version: v3.0  
  
Rolls back a database transaction started with sqlbegintran.  
  

### **20.13 SqlCommitTran**

  
*procedure SqlCommitTran;*  
  
From version: v3.0  
  
Commits a database transaction started with command sqlbegintran.  
  

### **20.14 SqlBindEx**

  
*procedure SqlBindEx(var x : string; size:integer);*  
  
From version: v3.0  
  
Links a program variable with a specified column size to SQL Server data when using SQLFetch.   
  
This is recommended instead of the SQLBind function if the value of the MaxBlobSize parameter is more than 80000 bytes (80 kb).   
  

### **20.15 SqlBeginEx**

  
*procedure SqlBeginEx(sSQL,sServer,sDatabase,sUser,sPwd:string);*  
  
From version: 350  
  
Prepares to execute a sql statment against a specified database.  
If you want to run a query against the current site database you can specify site as server and database and empty username and pasword.   
  
Examples:  
//Call any sql server database  
s1 := 'select ItemID from catalog';  
SqlBeginEx(s1,'10.100.100.100','ReportServer','sa','eProcurment');  
  
//To run a query against site repository  
s1 := 'select props from yct where wctxt =' + ToSQL('ohdo');  
SqlBeginEx(s1,'site','site','','');  
  

### **20.16 SqlExecuteInfo**

  
*function SqlExecuteInfo ( InfoAbout : string ) : string;*  
  
From version: 3.5.2L  
  
Fetch info about last SqlExecute:  
  
Message( SqlExecuteInfo( 'stmt' ) ); // show sql stmt  
Message( SqlExecuteInfo( 'info' ) ); // show info about result set and warnings...  
  

21 String management
--------------------

### **21.1 copy**

  
*function copy(s:string;idx,cnt:longint) : string;*  
  
Returns characters from a string from a specified start position and with a specified number of characters.  
  
Example: str1 := Copy('abcde', 3, 2); ==> str1 = 'cd'  
  

### **21.2 chr**

  
*function chr(i:integer) : string;*  
  
Returns a string of one character, which contains a specified ANSI character.  
  
Example:   
  
Function slask:boolean;  
var s1:string;  
  
Begin  
s1:=Chr(65);  
message(s1);  
End;  
  
This shows a message dialog with the letter A.  
  

### **21.3 ord**

  
*function ord(s : string) : integer;*  
  
Returns the ANSI value for the first character in 's'. If 's' contains an empty string, zero is returned.  
  
Example: int1 := Ord('A');  
  

### **21.4 length**

  
*function length(s : string) : LongInt;*  
  
Returns the length of a string.  
  
Example: str1 := Length( 'abcdef' );  
  

### **21.5 pos**

  
*function pos(substr,s:string):integer;*  
  
Returns the position of the first occurrence of 'substr' in 's'. Return value zero means that 'substr' is not found in 's'.  
  
Example: int1 := Pos('d', 'abcdef');  
  

### **21.6 SubStr**

  
*function SubStr(source: string; idx: integer; cnt: integer): string;*  
  
Returns the substring from the string (s) starting at a specified position (i) and with the number of characters specified (c).  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] source (String from where the substring will be retrieved)- [in] idx (Start position)- [in] cnt (Number of characters that will be retrieved)

  
Result:  
Desired substring  
  
Example:  
SubStr('abc', 2, 2) --> 'bc'  
SubStr('abc', 2, 1000) --> 'bc'  
SubStr('abc', 5, 2) --> '' Error  
SubStr('abc', -5, 2) --> '' Error  
  

### **21.7 Stuff**

  
*function Stuff(source: string; start: integer; length: integer; ins: string): string;*  
  
An advanced string manipulation function.  
  
Deletes [length] character from [source] from [start], and then inserts [ins] in [source] at position [start].  
  
Example:  
  
Stuff('Fredrik is smartest!', 1, 7, 'Sally')   
--> 'Sally is smartest!'  
  
To insert a string in another one in 'replace mode', do the following:  
  
s1 := 'pappa';  
Stuff( 'Hi mamma', 4, 5, length(s1), s1);  
--> 'Hi pappa'  
  

### **21.8 CodeTableConvert**

  
*function CodeTableConvert(sInput: string; iCodeTable: integer): string;*  
  
Converts an entered string using a specified code table.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sInput (String to convert)- [in] iCodeTable (Code table. 5 ==> Swedish)

  
Result:  
Converted string.  
  
=7D  
=7B  
=7C  
=5D  
=5B  
=5C  
  

### **21.9 ExtractString**

  
*function ExtractString(sString,sDelim: string; iPos : integer) : string;*  
  
From version: 32 v135  
  
Retrieves a string from a specified position in a separated string. If you send 1 in the position parameter, the total number of strings is returned.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] sString (String)- [in] sDelim (Separator)- [int] iPos (Desired position)

  
Example:  
where   
begin  
sText := ExtractString('Steve$Fredrik$Kalle','$',2);  
(\*sText=Fredrik\*)  
End;  
  

### **21.10 UpperCase**

  
*function UpperCase( s : string ) : string;*  
  
From version: 2.0  
  
Returnerar angiven strng i form av endast versaler  
  
Ex.  
UpperCase('Jeeves') --> 'JEEVES'  
  

### **21.11 LowerCase**

  
*function LowerCase( s : string ) : string;*  
  
From version: 2.0  
  
Returns a specific string in only lower case form.  
  
Ex.  
LowerCase('Jeeves') --> 'jeeves'  
  

### **21.12 StrComp**

  
*function StrComp( Str1, Str2 : string): Integer;*  
  
From version: 2.0  
  
A function to compare a text string, when you want to take into account small and big letters.   
Normal test in the macro language consider that small and big letter have the same values (if 'aaa' = 'AAA' then...).  
  
Return value      Condition  
  
<0      Str1 sorts before Str2  
=0      Str1is the same as Str2  
>0      Str1 sorts after Str2  
  
message(StrComp('A','B')); ==>> -1  
message(StrComp('A','A')); ==>> 0  
message(StrComp('B','A')); ==>> 1  
message(StrComp('a','A')); ==>> -1

From version: 2  
  
Delete spaces at the beginning of a string.

*function LTrim( s : string) : string;*

From version: 232 b

### **21.18 STR**

  
*function STR( NumValue:real; length:integer; decimals:Integer ) : string;*  
  
From version: 3.5.2  
  
Function for formatting a numeric value.  
Example:  
Message( '<' + STR( '1234.45', -1, -1 ) + '>' ); // ==>> < 1.23445000000000E+0003>  
Message( '<' + STR( '1234.45', 10, -1 ) + '>' ); // ==>> < 1.2E+0003>  
Message( '<' + STR( '1234.45', 10, 0 ) + '>' ); // ==>> < 1234'  
Message( '<' + STR( '1234.45', 10, 2 ) + '>' ); // ==>> < 1234.45>

### **21.20 ExecSqlOutput2FileEx**

  
*function ExecSqlOutput2FileEx ( SqlStmt : string; FileName : string; AddLfCr : boolean; Encoding:string; ColumnSeparator:string ) : LongInt;*  
  
From version: 3.5.2L  
  
Creates a text file from the output of the provided sql statment and there are no limit to the number of columns.  
If more than one column and no columnseparator is specified the function will add spaces.  


- AddLfCr - If true a new line is added for every record.- Encoding - Can be empty (which means ASCII) or utf8 or utf16- ColumnSeparator - adds this character between every column.

  
  
  

22 User interaction
-------------------

### **22.1 YesNo**

  
*function YesNo(s : string) : boolean;*  
  
Shows a dialog that contains specified text and Yes or No buttons. True is returned if the user presses Yes, otherwise False. The default focus on the confirmation dialog is set to Yes.  
  
Example:   
  
function Get\_Password: boolean;  
var  
sPrompt:string;  
status:boolean;  
begin  
Getstring('Enter Your Name',sPrompt);  
message (sPrompt);  
status:=yesno('Name is correct');  
end;  
  

### **22.2 Message**

  
*procedure Message(text : string);*  
  
Shows a dialog with a message according to a specified string and an OK button.  
  
Example: Message('Hi Lasse!');  
  
Note that beginning with version 2.0 \n is no longer processed as a row break. To make a row break, instead write chr(13) + chr(10).  
  

### **22.3 GetString**

  
*function GetString(Prompt : string;var s : string) : boolean;*  
  
Shows a dialog with a static question/text message, an Edit field and OK or CANCEL buttons. When the function is called, 's' can be set to a suitable default value. True is returned if the user closes the dialog by pressing OK, otherwise False is returned.  
  
Example: bool1 := GetString( 'Do you want to go home?', str1);  
  

### **22.4 LoadString**

  
*function LoadString(idx: integer): string;*  
  
Loads a resource string with index according to 'idx' from the current language table.  
  
Example: str1 := LoadString(8014);  
  

### **22.5 beep**

  
*procedure beep;*  
  
Produces sound, e.g. beep, in an integral speaker.  
  
Note that this macro function is not implemented for the Desktop client.  
  

### **22.6 NoYes**

  
*function NoYes(s : string) : boolean;*  
  
Shows a dialog with specified text and Yes or No buttons. True is returned if the user presses the Yes button, otherwise False. The default focus on the confirmation dialog is set to No.  
  
  
Example:  
  
function Get\_Password: boolean;  
var  
sPrompt:string;  
status:boolean;  
begin  
Getstring('Enter Your Name',sPrompt);  
message (sPrompt);  
status:=noyes('Name is correct');  
end;  
  

### **22.7 GetPassword**

  
*function GetPassword(sPrompt : string; var sResult: string) : boolean;*  
  
Displays an entry dialog (as does GetString) where the user can type in a text, where every entered character displays as an asterisk.  
  
Example:  
  
function Get\_Password: boolean;  
var  
sPrompt:string;  
sString:String;  
begin  
GetPassword('Enter the Password',sPrompt);  
Message ('your password is' + sPrompt),  
end;  
  

### **22.8 MultiGetString**

  
*function MultiGetString(Header, Delim, Prompt, Def, NullValue : string;var s : string) : boolean;*  
  
From version: 135  
  
Shows a dialog box with several questions/text messages, and an associated field and OK or CANCEL buttons. When the function is called, 's' must be set to a suitable default value. The function returns True if the user closes the dialog by pressing OK, else it returns False.  
  
At the beginning of the parameter Def (for default values) you can include a type of field of your choice you would like to have and without specification a standard edit field will be shown.  
  
Possible values for field types:  
<%CHECKBOX>  
Creates a checkbox control  
<%COMBO>  
Creates a drop-down list control that is automatically sorted. The different options should be supplied in the default values with char 13 as separator.  
<%COMBOUNSORTED>  
Same as Combo except that the items is not automatically sorted but instead is displayed in the order they are supplied.  
<%MEMO>  
Creates a memo control that makes it possible to write multiple lines of texts.  
<%LABEL>  
Creates a label control to display static text.  
<%EDITDATE>  
Editdate creates an edit box with the date formatted according to the client windows settings and attached calendar that the user can choose from.  
The control expects to receive any default date in yyyyMMdd format and will also return the date in this format.  
<%EDITNUMBER>  
Editnumer creates an edit box that is restricted to only edit (and displaying) numbers. The default value should only contain numbers and if applicable a decimal separator (comma or dot doesn't matter).  
The maximum number of decimal that is possible to enter is decided by how many decimals that the default value contained and the decimal separator displayed is same as what   
the user has chosen in Windows.  
If the result contains decimal it will always be in the form of a period.  
  
Macro example:  
sHeader := 'Specify personal data';  
sSeparator := '$';  
sFieldPrompts := 'FirstName$LastName$Age$Gender$Instruction';  
sDefaultValues := 'Write your first name here...$Write your last name here...$Write your age here...$<%COMBO>Man'+Chr(13)+Female+'$<%LABEL>Click OK';  
sCharIfNull := chr(85);  
multigetstring(sHeader, Separator, sFieldPrompts, sDefaultValues, sCharIfNull, sResult);  
  
It is possible to add a new row break char(13) in the Header parameters so that the remaining portion of the text will be displayed at the top of the dialog box. For example, this can be used for help text.  
  
You can specify #CtrlWidth=250# - with the desired value, of course - in the header parameter. In this way, all controls to the right of the field prompt can be assigned the desired width (otherwise, a value of 160 applies). Drop-down lists also have dynamic width according to the longest text when opened, in the same way as in Jeeves standard forms.

23 Version information
----------------------

### **23.1 GetVersion**

  
*function GetVersion(iProgramCode:integer):string;*  
  
From version: 32 v131  
  
Retrieves version information for the specified program.  
  
**Parameter description:**

- [in] iProgramCode (Constant that specifies which programs version information will be retrieved)

  
Constants:  
JEEVES\_KERNEL = 0  
JEEVES\_DB = 1  
JEEVES\_KERNEL\_PLATTFORM = 2  
  
JEEVES\_SERVER\_COMM\_PROTOCOL\_VERSION = 3  
JEEVES\_SERVER\_KERNEL\_SUBVERSION = 4  
  
JEEVES\_CLIENT\_KERNEL\_VERSION = 5  
  
JEEVES\_SERVER\_KERNEL\_BUILDNUMBER = 6  
  
Beginning with version 5.1 R5  
JEEVES\_SERVER\_KERNEL\_VERSION = 7  
  

### **23.2 GetJMLPlattform**

  
*function GetJMLPlattform : integer;*  
  
From version: 32 v133  
  
Returns the platform number for Jeeves Kernel.  
  
Return values:  
16 = Earlier classic client (obsolete)  
32 = Classic client  
  
This is used to make macros different depending on the kernel/server version. It can also be used to avoid the use of functions, which are specific to a newer kernel/server version, in an earlier one.  
  

### **23.3 GetDBInfo**

  
*function GetDBInfo( iCode : integer ) : string;*  
  
From version: 32 v1.50  
  
Displays information on the database.  
  
0 = database name for the application  
1 = database name for site repository  
2 = name of server (@@ServerName)  
3 = version of SQL Server (@@Version)  
  

### **23.4 GetUserInfo**

  
*function GetUserInfo( iCode : integer ) : string;*  
  
From version: 32 v1.50  
  
Retrieve the value of specified parameter.  
  
0 = Print to screen (returns 0 = not checked 1=checked)  
1 = Current language code  
2 = Client side default printer  
3 = Client side computer name  
4 = ShortName of clients current language ( 'GB', 'FR', ... -->> Lang\_GB, Lang\_FR, ... )  
(5 = gcTimeZone)  
(6 = GetTimeZone)  
7 = client signature  
8 =   

0= ordinary(not JavaGC)

1= JavaGC

  
9 = Type of client (thin, rich)  
10 = Unique client identifier  
  
11= Realclient type  

0: (cltStandardThin)

1: (cltStandardRich)

2: (cltJavaGC)

3: (cltNewClient)

  
12 = Crystal report file path  
13 = Type of ExportDestination set by the user in Print settings dialog in Jeeves  
14 = Current company ID (sy1.foretagkod)


  

**This chapter is only provided in English.**

**This chapter is only provided in English.**

There is a large number of parameters that can be set up by system administrators or the like to control how Jeeves should function in general. This includes parameters about how the database is set up, how the client should behave and so on. The parameters can be set per company, group and/or user, depending on the parameter.  
  
Jeeves loads a default value for parameters that are not set. However, certain parameters must be set, most notably the database-related parameters.  
  
You set up the parameters in the Kernel parameters program (jini). In this chapter they are described according to the following convention:  
  
**[Section]**  
 **Parameter**  
 Default value:  
 Description  
  
**Switches to Classic client:**  
 /lic - Apply license  
  
/nosplash - Splash screen does not appear at client startup  
  
/r - Start with a specific program  
  
/menuid - Click on a menu item  
  
/batch\_runonce - Print process in a batch  
  
/RunMacro - Run the PostRunMacro macro command with the macro unique ID provided in the parameter, for example /RunMacro{41f866bb-069d-402d-a192-1c4b18bae381}. Note! The macro needs to be saved as a global macro. No macros linked to the event At log on will be run when using this switch.  
  
/p - Password. Enter password at client startup.  
  
/U - User. Enter username at client startup.  
  
/s - Signature. Enter login signature at client startup.  
  
**Switches to Desktop client:**  
You can specify the following login switches that are sent as parameters to the client at startup:  
  
/p - Password. Enter password at client startup.  
  
/U - User. Enter username at client startup.  
  
/s - Signature. Enter login signature at client startup.  
  
/S - Startup parameter. Supplies the server as a start-up parameter, making it possible to configure different shortcuts or command-lines to different servers with the same installation. The startup parameter can have different configuration options, as follows: /S{Server entry}|{Server}:{port}(:{connectiontype}(:{securitymode})).   
 You can supply a server with this parameter as follows:   
 - by entering the server element name referring to connecttoserver.xml; for example: Jeeves.ERPClient.exe /SJeeves 5.1 SP. Note that the value of this parameter must be enclosed within quotation marks if the name contains spaces.  
 or  
 - by entering the Server (dns name or ip), with optional port, connection type, and security mode; for example:   
 /Skernel51spman:4502  
 /S198.162.92.176:4502  
 Note that when using Server (dns name or ip) and the optional parameters, the entries in connecttoserver.xml are not used and the securitymode and connection type will have default values.  
 Once the startup parameter is passed to the client, the server connection is initiated before the Login dialog is displayed.   
  
The default values specified in the switches are entered in the login input fields. If all fields have default values, the user will be automatically logged in.  

1 CrystalReport
---------------

### **1.1 ConditionAlert**

  
Version:  
Default value = N only global setting  
Specifies whether a warning will be given when printing Crystal Reports if no restriction has been made by flagging fields in the form.  
  
Possible values:  
Y = Warning given  
N = No warning  
  

### **1.2 ReportPath**

  
Version:2.0  
Global parameter only  
Specifies the directory path to where the crystal reports are saved. Previously the directory path was set in the Jeeves Master database but from kernel 2.0 it is used only in cases where the jini parameter has not been set.  
  

2 Database
----------

### **2.1 DaysToSaveMailLog**

  
Version:  
Global parameter only  
  

### **2.2 DataBase**

The name of the database in question.  

### **2.3 DBLibrary**

  
Version:  
Default value = NTWDBLIB.DLL only global setting  
Name of the DB Library file.  
  

### **2.4 MaxBlobSize**

  
Version:  
Default value = 80 000 bytes  
Maximum length of data that can be written in fields of the Binary Large Object type. The greater the value specified, the more memory is required to run Jeeves.  
  
Recommendation:  
A single SQLBind(string) function call will by default request memory according to the value of this parameter. This value will be multiplied by as many SQLBind calls for string variables that exist, which can result in an insufficient buffer issue.  
  
We recommend that you use the SQLBindEx macro function in application logic for binding String type of variables. This API provides an option to specify the length of the string to be bound. Using this API you can control the amount of memory buffer requested by the kernel internally, thus avoiding any issue with insufficient buffer.  
  

### **2.5 MaxDBProcesses**

  
Version:v2.0.4  
Global parameter only  
Not used from kernel versions 3.0 and higher.  
  
Decides how many databases processes Jeeves will setup when starting. Do not set this unless there are entries in the log file suggesting this.  
  

### **2.6 OptimisticLocking**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Specifies whether Optimistic locking will be on or off.  
  
If the parameter is on, the kernel checks if the current record has been changed since it was loaded into the form. If the record has been changed the message "No hits in the database when updating table" is displayed.  
  
The purpose is to avoid writing over other users' changes to the same database record.  
  

### **2.7 SecurityMode**

  
Version:  
Default value = 0  
Specifies which type of authorization Jeeves shall use:  
0 = Default SQL Login  
1 = Windows user authentication against SQL Server and sy2, then SQL Login  
2 = Windows user authentication against SQL Server and sy2  
3 = Windows user authentication against sy2, then SQL Login  
4 = Windows user authentication against sy2  
5 = Windows user authentication against SID stored in Jeeves  
  
For type 3, 4, and 5, you must use the JvsAdminFunction table to assign admin functions to a user.  
  
If your system is not set up for single sign-on, see Login ID/name (Field: dbloginID).  
  

### **2.8 Select with (NOLOCK)**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Y enables reading of locked records in the database, which increases performance.  
This only applies to database selects used when running reports.  
  

### **2.9 SiteRepository**

  
Version:  
Default value = Enligt parametern Database only global setting  
The name of the Site Repository database, i.e. the one that contains settings, modifications and supplements that are done by a user or administrator.  
  

### **2.10 SiteRepositoryTableCreator**

Signature for 'Table creator' in the Site Repository database. The information is only needed if the signature is other than 'Database owner'.
  
  

### **2.11 SQLLoockGard**

  
Version:32 v135  
Default value = 0  
Logs SQL transactions that take longer in seconds than specified by the parameter.   
  
0 specifies that the function is switched off.  
  
If a database execution takes longer, an SQL clause and the result set from the SQL procedure sp\_blocker\_pss are logged.  
This procedure specifies a database lock associated with the current 'spid' (database process).  
  
The result is entered in the JeevesPerformance.txt file.  
  

### **2.12 SQLServer**

  
Version:  
Global parameter only  
The name of the SQL server.  
  

### **2.13 Sysprotects**

Name of indexed table to read sysprotects from. The Sysprotects table in SQL Server is not indexed which can cause performance problems.
  
  

### **2.14 TableCreator**

  
Version:  
Default value = dbo  
Signature for the user who created (and 'owns') the tables in the database.  
  

### **2.15 TestDatabase**

  
Version:32 v1.50  
Default value = N  
All printouts made from databases with this parameter set will see the text "TEST" printed across the page.  
This is to be able to distinguish printouts from test databases and correct databases. If a database is dumped  
and then loaded into a new database, the new database will treat it as a test database and  
treat it as such. This parameter cannot be used to close off the text "TEST" in  
such a database but only activate text in such databases not automatically treated as a  
test database.  
  

### **2.16 UserName**

The name of who you want as default when logging onto the database.  

### **2.17 UseConsistencyChecks**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Y = activates consistency checks in triggers in the Jeeves database.  
N = deactivates the consistency checks in triggers in the Jeeves database. It is suggested that you only set this parameter to N if you do not want to perform consistency checks. However, when running macros consistency checks are always enabled irrespective of the value in this parameter.  
  
This function is only applicable if the Database Compatibility Level is equal to or greater than 130, indicating that Jeeves ERP is deployed on SQL Server 2016 or higher.  
  

### **2.18 UseTempDBForReportSelect**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
If hit number during report batch is greater than the specified number, the result is entered in a temporary table and is then read from there. The parameter is used to reduce the number of lockings in the system.  
Y = 500  
  

### **2.19 UseRestrFromListWin**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Parameter that you can use to retain behavior from earlier versions of the kernel regarding print selections. The kernel now uses the restrictions from the list window IF a report is started from the list window.  
  
In earlier versions the report's definition controlled the print selections. If a report was printed from a program with strict restrictions (e.g. only closed orders), but the report's definition was less strict, other records were also included in the printout. The same applied when right-clicking and printing reports.  
  

### **2.20 ViewsOnRelatedTables**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Y = Restrictive views also apply for related tables and not just the base table in the program.  
  

### **2.21 JeevesMaster**

Version:   
Default value = JeevesMaster  
Specifies the database in which metadata for SSRS/Crystal reports is stored.   
  

3 DesktopClient
---------------

### **3.1 ClassicModeAutogen**

  
Version:  
Default value = 0 or N (false)  
Specifies if the server should use the Classic mode or not when auto generating the XAML code.  
  
A value of 1 or Y (true) means that the server should use the Classic mode.  
  

### **3.2 ClassicModeAdjustMargin**

  
Version:  
Default value = 1 or Y (true)  
Specifies if the margins in the program form should be adjusted to resemble the look in the Classic client. Normally, this should be set to Y (true), which means the margins in the program form on the Desktop client will resemble those in the Classic client.  
  
Note that this setting has no effect if the ClassicModeAutogen parameter is set to false.  
  

### **3.3 ClassicModeFieldStretch**

  
Version:  
Default value = 0 or N (false)  
Specifies if the fields should be stretched within a column or have the same width as in the Classic client.  
  
A value of 1 or Y (true) means that the fields will be stretched within the column.  
  
Note that this setting has no effect if the ClassicModeAutogen parameter is set to false.  
  

### **3.4 DashboardFontSize**

Controls the font size of all the widgets displayed on the dashboard. This functionality can also be set at the widget level using the UserFontSize property. The value set at the widget level takes priority over that set at the dashboard level.  

### **3.5 UserClientHideUnboundObjects**

  
Version:3.5.2f  
Default value = 1  
Specifies if unbound objects, such as fields in forms and columns in lists, should be hidden/invisible or shown/visible in the Desktop client. By unbound objects we mean objects that, for some reason, are considered incorrectly defined either by the client or the Jeeves server. This can, for example, be a field with an incorrectly defined ID or that is missing in the database.  
  
- Parameter data = 0 means the object will be shown/visible and marked in order to indicate that the design contains an unbound object.  
- Parameter data = 1 means the object will be hidden/invisible (default value).  
  

### **3.6 ShowErrorMessageOnListBindFailed**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Specifies whether an error message is displayed when a program is opened if an incorrect design exists in an underlying list; i.e. if there is a difference in window context, node, and/or program name of the underlying lists compared with that of the program form.  
  
Possible values:  
Y = Error message is shown if an incorrect design exists in an underlying list.  
N = Error message is not shown even if an incorrect design exists in an underlying list.  
  

4 Fonts
-------

### **4.1 DefFontBold**

Specifies whether the standard font in Jeeves should be in bold or not (Y/N). Only takes effect if a default font name is specified.  

### **4.2 DefFontName**

The name of the font wanted as default in Jeeves.  

### **4.3 DefFontSize**

The size of the font wanted as default in Jeeves. Only takes effect if a default font name is specified.  

5 Insight
---------

### **5.1 UserClientHideUnboundObjects**

  
Version:3.5.2f  
Default value = 1  
Specifies if unbound objects, such as fields in forms and columns in lists, should be hidden/invisible or shown/visible in the Insight user client. By unbound objects we mean objects that, for some reason, are considered incorrectly defined either by the client or the Jeeves server. This can, for example, be a field with an incorrectly defined ID or that is missing in the database.  
  
- Parameter data = 0 means the object will be shown/visible and marked in order to indicate that the design contains an unbound object.  
- Parameter data = 1 means the object will be hidden/invisible (default value).  
  

### **5.2 ReportBaseUrl**

\*\*\* NO LONGER APPLICABLE \*\*\*  
  
The base URL from clients point of view to download the report PDF  

### **5.3 ReportServerPath**

\*\*\* NO LONGER APPLICABLE \*\*\*  
  
The path from the Jeeves Servers point of view, where to create the report PDF
  

6 Jeeves
--------

### **6.1 AddModeOnSearch**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Puts the form in new entry mode (add mode) if no hit is found during the search.  
  

### **6.2 AllowLoggOnAsDBO**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
N = Allows no users to log in as database owner, dbo (sa).  
  

### **6.3 ApplicationDirectory**

  
Version:  
Global parameter only  
Path to Jeeves application directory.  
  

### **6.4 Authority**

This parameter is used to set the URL of the identity service that will authorize the federated login process. The value entered here must match with the URL generated from the admin console for the identity service.  

### **6.5 BackImage**

Indicates name and path (from the server's point of view) to the file that will be used as background in Jeeves.  
If you set up parameterdata = N instead of a file path then the product line image behind the form/list windows
will not show.
  

### **6.6 BackWebPage**

This parameter is used for setting a web page as background in Jeeves. In the parameter data field you enter the address to the web page, for example: http://www.jeeves.se  
  
You can specify the following placeholders in the url:  
 %language%   
 %perssign%  
 %foretagkod%  
 which will be replaced by current values when the client starts up.  
  
Example:  
http://jvsstofraa03/test/default.asp?foretagkod=%foretagkod%&language=%language%&perssign=%perssign%  
  
Note! It is important that the Jeeves client has access to the path specified in this parameter.  

### **6.7 BlockWildSearch**

  
Version:v2.1  
Default value = 0  
Parameter to prevent the use of wild searches (i.e. without a search condition) which generate a lot of hits.  
  
Jeeves will normally only display a maximum of 1000 rows. A user can however manually change this value to make Jeeves display more or fewer hits in a program during a session.  
  
If BlockWildSearch is turned on and you perform a wild search in a program where the hit result exceeds the limit, a record will be added to the Jini table. If it is done in the Order1 program it would look like this:  
  
Parameter section: BlockWildSearch  
Parameter: oh  
Parameter data: 1   
  
This record will prevent wild searches in all programs in which the Order header table (oh) is the main table. If you attempt to do a wild search in such programs you will get a message saying that it is not allowed. You can turn it off by setting the parameter data to 0.  
  
  
Set up the BlockWildSearch parameter in Jini as follows:  
  
Parameter section: Jeeves  
Parameter: BlockWildSearch  
Parameter data: 1  
  

### **6.8 CheckBoxStyle**

By default parameterdata=0, which means that user added fields of datatype ztboolean will be
shown as checkbox. If you wish for the fields to be shown as fields with the possible values Y/ N,
you set up this parameter in jini with parameterdata=1.  
You can also set parameterdata=2, then jeeves will also show standard jeeves checkbox fields as
editfields.  

### **6.9 CheckPrinttoEDM**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Parameter that defines if the Print to EDM functionality is enabled. If this functionality is enabled, the system automatically creates EDM records for all reports that have been set up for printout to EDM.  
  

### **6.10 ConvCRWhere**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Y = Convert double quotation marks (") to single quotation marks (') in search filters that are sent to Crystal Reports or SSRS reports.  
  

### **6.11 ClientCacheSourceFolder**

This parameter applies only to Desktop client and Thin client.  
  
Specifies the directory path on the server where files that need to be distributed (mainly report files and images used in Jeeves standard reports) to all connected clients are stored. This parameter is used for file sharing between the business server and the client.  
  
When the file path is specified in the Parameter data field and you start the Jeeves client, Jeeves initiates a file comparison between the files stored in the specified folder on the server and those in the ClientCache folder in the client. It then generates a list of files which are changed on the server or missing on the client and sends the list to the server, which streams the files to the ClientCache folder on the client.  
  
Note that to enable distribution of content from the server to all clients, a mirror of the ClientCache folder has to be created manually on the server.  

### **6.12 CCUAutoLogOutTime**

A concurrent user logged into Jeeves is automatically logged off and the client session is closed if the session remains idle for the time (in minutes) specified in the Parameter data field.  
  
Note that the idle time is determined from when the user launches the application and not from when the user is logged into the application.  
  
The close dialog displays the following message: You have been logged out due to inactivity.  

### **6.13 DBMS**

  
Version:  
Default value = SQLServer  
Specifies which type of database is used, currently only SQL Server.  
  

### **6.14 DecimalSeparator**

This parameter is no longer used (as of kernel version 4.0). From this version the decimal separator is set via a dialog opened from Tools, Settings, General... and is stored in the site repository. See the chapter on settings on the Tools menu.  

### **6.15 DefaultBackgroundColor**

  
Version:v2.1.0  
Global parameter only  
With this parameter you can specify the default background color in Jeeves. The value entered in parameter data should be a hash mark (#) followed by a hexadecimal number. It will affect the background in the form and the area behind the form window.   
  
In kernel v2.1.0 the default background color was changed to white. If you wished to have the classic grey color (Windows XP) you set up this parameter with the hexadecimal number ECE9D8.  
  
As of kernel v3.0.1 the default background color follows the current Windows theme. If no change has been made to the Windows theme, it will be grey on Classic, XP and Vista themes. If you would like default white background, you can set this parameter to #FFFFFF.  
  
You can also change the color of the form with the new site repository setting (Tools, Settings, Background color), this setting will however not affect the area behind the list and form windows.  
  

### **6.16 DefaultDateMask**

This parameter is no longer used (as of kernel version 4.0). From this version the date format is set via a dialog opened from Tools, Settings, General... and is stored in the site repository. See the chapter on settings on the Tools menu.  

### **6.17 DefaultMoneyMask**

This parameter is no longer used (as of kernel version 4.0). From this version the currency format is set via a dialog opened from Tools, Settings, General... and is stored in the site repository. See the chapter on settings on the Tools menu.  

### **6.18 DefaultNumericMask**

This parameter is no longer used (as of kernel version 4.0). From this version the numeric format is set via a dialog opened from Tools, Settings, General... and is stored in the site repository. See the chapter on settings on the Tools menu.  

### **6.19 DevMenu**

1 means that a special menu containing functions for developers displays under File.  
0 means that the menu is hidden.  

### **6.20 DropListCache**

  
Version:1.5.6  
Default value = 0  
Makes it possible to limit the cache to reduce memory consumption on the server.  
- If it is set to an optional number over 0, the list view is cleared each time you exit a program and the number of records in the list exceeds the specified quantity.  
- If it is set to 1, one record will be keep, that correspons to the current record in the form.  
- If it is set to -1 both form and list will be cleared.  
  

### **6.21 EDMProgram**

  
Version:32 v135  
Default value = pdmnv only global setting  
Specifies which program will start when you click on the command button for document management.  
  

### **6.22 EnableCacheForReportPrinting**

  
Version:  
Default value = 35000  
Controls the use of the cache buffer while loading and populating records in the Reprint invoice (rFhUtskr) report. Cache will not be used if the no. of resultant records exceeds the specified value.  
  
It is recommended that you use this parameter with care as it can impact Jeeves performance.  
  

### **6.23 ForcePrinter**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
For printouts linked to print rules, the program can switch templates during the actual printing. Each template can be saved with its own printer selection. If you want the selected printer to apply to all documents, regardless of the printer selection for the template, this parameter must be set to "Y".  
  

### **6.24 FederatedClientID**

This parameter is used to set the client ID for federated login. The value is entered manually and it must match the client ID generated from the admin console for the identity service.  

### **6.25 FormCondInReport**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Y means that you only need to enter a search filter directly in the form as selection to print a report.  
N means that you must also perform a search for the selection to apply.   
  
If you set N, you reduce the risk of printing a report covering a large number of records through accidental flagging in a form.  
  
If this parameter is set, you need to take care when selecting fields, otherwise more orders, invoices, etc. than expected might be included in the printout.  
  

### **6.26 Jeeves\_InvNo\_JvsType**

  
Version:v2.1  
Global parameter only  
Should contain the word bigint if having the Invoice number (FaktNr...) declared as BigInt in the database  
  

### **6.27 Jeeves\_VchrNo\_JvsType**

  
Version:v2.1  
Global parameter only  
Should contain the word bigint if having the Voucher number (VerNr...) declared as BigInt in the database  
  

### **6.28 JeevesERPServer**

This parameter is used to set the URL of the Jeeves cloud ERP server. If the URL is specified, the Desktop client retrieves the data that is displayed in the dashboard widgets from the Jeeves cloud ERP server.
  
  

### **6.29 FrameWorkVersion**

Parameter that can be used to override the default CLR version that is being used when running .Net integration. The following options are available:  
  
- 11 for CLR version 1.1 used by .Net Framework 1.1  
 - 20 for CLR version 2.0 used by .Net Framework 2.0 - 3.5  
 - 40 for CLR version 4.0 used by .Net Framework 4.0 and 4.5  

### **6.30 FrameWorkVersion**

Parameter that can be used to override the default CLR version that is being used when running .Net integration. The following options are available:  
  
- 11 for CLR version 1.1 used by .Net Framework 1.1  
 - 20 for CLR version 2.0 used by .Net Framework 2.0 - 3.5  
 - 40 for CLR version 4.0 used by .Net Framework 4.0 and 4.5  

### **6.31 LoggIPIntervall**

  
Version:32 v135  
Default value = 0  
This function logs the response time for a ping (to and from) between a server and client in the file Performance.txt. The interval is specified in milliseconds.  
  
You can use this function to measure the network's response time between server and client. Note that measurement should be performed on unloaded machines so that the load does not influence measurement. If the server is loaded, measurement can be performed between an unused client and an unloaded machine that sits on the same switch/hub.  
  
0 specifies that the function is switched off.  
  

### **6.32 LRUCacheHigh**

  
Version:  
Default value = 5242880 Bytes (5 MB)  
Specifies a limit, in the form of available memory in bytes, when cache emptying will start. If you specify LRUCacheHigh = 0 and LRUCacheLow = 0, LRU caching is inactivated.  
  

### **6.33 LRUCacheLow**

  
Version:  
Default value = 10485760 Bytes (10 MB)  
Specifies a limit, in the form of available memory in bytes, when cache emptying will end. If you specify LRUCacheHigh = 0 and LRUCacheLow = 0, LRU caching is inactivated.  
  

### **6.34 LRUCacheMode**

  
Version:  
Default value = 1  
Specifies when inactive programs will start to be deleted from the cache:  
1 = When the physical memory is full  
2 = When the virtual memory is full  
  

### **6.35 MailType**

Specifies which e-mail system is used.  
  
Possible values:  
 - Outlook  

### **6.36 MaskOnDDEGcItem**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Y = Formats associated with the field are used for data.  
N = Formats associated with the field are not used for data.  
  

### **6.37 MaskOnGcItem**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Used instead of MaskOnDDEGcItem (loaded later by Jeeves Server).  
  
Default value = Y  
Y = Formats associated with the field are used for data.  
N = Formats associated with the field are not used for data.  
  

### **6.38 MenuDescription**

Not normally used. (Exceptionally to name the file that describes the menu's structure if there is no menu in the 'Menu' table.)  

### **6.39 MinimizeResources**

  
Version:  
Default value = 0  
1 = Reduces use of resources by deleting fields in inactive windows. For 9.x environments.  
  

### **6.40 MultipleMacroConnectedToEvent**

  
Version:4.0  
Default value = Y  
Allows multiple macros connected to the same event, as long as the event is not saved on the same dimension.  
  
If this is turned off, it will work in the same manner as in kernels previous to the 4.0 version, in that only one macro connection is executed.  
  
If there are several possible macro connections to the same event, the connection stored on a site repository dimension of the highest priority is executed.  
  

### **6.41 MultiCompany**

Y means that the database is a multi-company database.  
N means that the database is a single company database.  
  
For more information, see the different chapters under Multi company handling in the online documentation.  

### **6.42 MultiCompanySearchSave**

  
Version:v3.0.2  
Default value = N only global setting  
The parameter indicates if the company IDs specified in the multi company search function should be saved between user sessions.  
  
If set to 'Y' the company IDs and company intervals are saved when set by the user. When the user starts a new session the search condition is added to the search menu and set as the active search condition.  
If set to 'N' the multi company search function acts as before, i.e. the company IDs and company intervals are not saved between sessions.  
  

### **6.43 AllowCrossCompanyReport**

  
Version:v3.0.2  
Default value = N only global setting  
Parameter to activate the menu option for multi-company searches in reports.  
  

### **6.44 CrossCompanyReportSave**

  
Version:v3.0.2  
Default value = N  
The parameter indicates if the company IDs specified in the multi company search for reports should be saved between user sessions.  
  
If set to 'Y' the company IDs and company intervals are saved when set by the user. When the user starts a new session the search condition is added to the search menu and set as the active search condition.  
If set to 'N' the multi company search function acts as before, i.e. the company IDs and company intervals are not saved between sessions.  
  

### **6.45 NrOfListRowsToPreload**

Specifies how many rows should be preloaded above and below the rows that are visible in the list viewport. The default value for this parameter is 10, but this value is configurable depending on user behavior and the (network) performance in the customer's Jeeves environment.  
  
Jeeves recommends that if you have a fast network connection between the Jeeves client and the Jeeves server and you do a lot of scrolling in the lists, you should increase this value to experience a smoother scrolling in the list.
  
  

### **6.46 NoRemoveOfMissingTerm**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Y = Suppress the query about removing terms added from tables which have the term missing in the table definition.  
  

### **6.47 NotificationUrl**

This parameter is used to set the notification service URL created by Jeeves Cloud operations for the mobile notification service.  

### **6.48 NotificationApiKey**

This parameter is used to set the API key generated in the Admin console by Jeeves Cloud operations for the mobile notification service.  

### **6.49 NumpadAsFunctionKeys**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Defines if the numerical keypad should be used for numbers or as function keys.  
Y = As function keys  
N = For digits  
  

### **6.50 OnCriticalError**

  
Version:  
Default value = 1  
Specifies when the server will be shut down for Critical Error, i.e. when the server cannot accept new clients due to an error:  
1= Shuts down the server when the last client finishes or has a Critical Error  
2 = Shuts down the server immediately  
  

### **6.51 PageOverflow\_Footer**

  
Version:  
Global parameter only  
If you set this parameter in jini to Y a sub-total will be printed at the bottom of the page, if applicable. (Introduced in standard Jeeves from version 11.0.)  
  

### **6.52 PageOverflow\_Header**

If you set this parameter in jini to Y a sub-total from the previous page will be printed at the top of the page, if applicable. (Introduced in standard Jeeves from version 11.0.)  

### **6.53 PayTerminalDLL**

Version:2.0.2  
Global parameter only  
Specifies the name on the dll that contains the pay terminal solution you want to run.   
  

### **6.54 PDFForceFontEmbedding**

  
Version:v3.0.3l  
Global parameter only  
Some fonts are not shown correctly in the pdf-file unless that font is installed on the computer   
that opens the file. As an example we have had problems with barcodes. Including all fonts   
in the file solves the problem but the downside is that the file can then become very large.   
  
We have therefore created this parameter in kernel v3.0.X (available as of hotfix v3.0.3l) that   
you can use to define the font that you want to have embedded in the pdf.   
Example parameter data = "Arial", "Microsoft Sans Serif"  
  
The parameter is only applicable in kernel v3.0.X. As of kernel version v3.5.1,   
the solution is to on the template (i.e. in the dialog where you create/modify your   
report templates) add the fonts that you wish to have embedded.   
  

### **6.55 PingAlive**

  
Version:v2.0.2 (i)  
Default value = Y  
Server controls that the client connection is still intact through use of a ping message.   
  
This parameter can be used to reactivate connections that were closed because of inactivity.   
  
Control interval: 60 seconds.  
  

### **6.56 QtyTruncDecIfZero**

  
Version:32 v1.50 Beta1  
Default value = N  
Specify that as few decimals as possible must be used to display the quantity field (qty). If a whole number, the decimal portion will be truncated completely. Takes effect in Forms, lists and reports.  
  
If a format has been defined the setting has no effect.  
  

### **6.57 ResetPrinterSettings**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
If you set this parameter to Y (true), any changes made in the printer dialog will be reset when a template (new or the same) is selected by the template editor. This means that changed printer settings, such as tray selection, number of copies etc., are not carried over to the selected template.  
  
If you set this parameter to N (false), the printer settings specified in the template are always used and they remain unchanged when a template (same or new) is selected.  
  
If this parameter is not created in the Kernel parameters (Jini) program, it will have the default value of N (false).  
  

### **6.58 RightClickBySa**

  
Version:  
Default value = Y  
Makes it possible to right-click (CRTL+E) for users with a dbo-login (sa) to another program missing on your own menu.  
  
If the parameter's value = Y, only users with a dbo login (sa) can right-click to another program not found on the menu.  
  
If the parameter's value = N this makes it possible to right-click (CTRL+E) to another program not found on the menu.  
  

### **6.59 SameTemplateSamePrintJob**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
If Y, the print batch (for example an invoice batch) is treated as a single print job in the printer. You can also specify the number of print jobs to be generated.  
  
**Example - invoice printout:**  
N means that each invoice generates an individual print job.  
Y means that all invoices in the batch are treated as a single print job.  
25 means that the printout is divided into 25 invoices per print job.  
  
  
**Note!**  
  
- If you do not select a template, i.e. choose the No template option, any print rules are ignored.  
  
- If you set up printing rules to direct different templates to different printers, the print rules will be ignored if you bundle multiple printouts by using the SameTemplateSamePrintJob kernel parameter.   
  
This also applies if you order several printouts with different templates to the same printer, i.e.:  
  
- If SameTemplateSamePrintJob=Y any print rules are ignored.  
  
- When making a screen print of multiple printouts, any print rules are ignored.  
  
Also note:  
- Fax connection demands that the linked template is connected to the fax printer.  
  

### **6.60 ShutDown**

  
Version:  
Default value = 1  
Specifies whether the menu option to close the server will be visible:  
0 = Never visible  
1 = Visible only for users logged in as database owner, dbo  
2 = Always visible  
  

### **6.61 SupportMailAddress**

The main address to which support mail will be sent from Jeeves support client. The address entered here is used as the default address in the Send feedback form.  

### **6.62 SupportReturnMail**

Specified return address in support mail.  

### **6.63 SupportMailType**

  
Version:  
Default value = SMTP  
Type of mail protocol for support mail.  
  

### **6.64 IntrnCoNoLastInIndex**

  
Version:v205  
Default value = Y  
By default Jeeves will put foretagkod last in an index (primary key).  
If you wish foretagkod to be put first in the index you can set up this jini parameter with parameter data: N  
This only applies to multi-company databases.  
  

### **6.65 XMLStreamFileEnabled**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Specifies if the functionality to use StreamServe when printing reports with the template editor in Jeeves should be active or not in the system for a specific user or for all users (\*).   
A file is saved on the server with all fields in XML format and StreamServe reads the file automatically.   
  
Y = the function for StreamServe adapter is active  
N = the function for StreamServe adapter is not active  
  

### **6.66 XMLStreamFileSavePath**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Specifies the directory path where the XML files are saved for a specific user or for all users (\*). If you do not specify a path the XML files will automatically be saved in c:/Jeeves\_xmloutput.  
  
For the StreamServe template package the correct search path should be in the Global project: StreamServe\Projects\Global\Export\Input  
  
The search path can have a maximum length of 100 characters.  
  

### **6.67 XMLSplitUpBlob**

  
Version:3.0.2p  
Default value = N  
Set this parameter to split up blob text when printing to XML.  
Each line in blob text is placed in an own tag.  
To enable set parameter to Y  
  

### **6.68 TactonLog**

  
Version:v2.3  
Default value = N only global setting  
When using the Tacton server integration in Jeeves it is possible to log the communication between Jeeves and the Tacton server. The logging is controlled by this jini parameter.   
  
When Y is entered in the field paramdata, the logging is activated and three logs, TCserverlog.txt, JvsTactonIntLog.txt and JvsTactonIntLogSIGN.txt, are generated in your server catalogue. JvsTactonIntLog.txt logs common events, for example the creation of the common factory. JvsTactonIntLogSIGN.txt is generated by each client where SIGN is the client's signature used in Jeeves. JvsTactonIntLogSIGN.txt logs the transactions between the Tacton Server and Jeeves for each client. TCServerlog.txt logs the transactions in the Tacton server.   
  
When N is entered in the field paramdata, the logging is deactivated and no logs will be generated. By default, the logging is turned off.  
  
Note that if you run the Tacton server as a service only JvsTactonIntLog.txt and JvsTactonIntLogSIGN.txt will be generated and possible to control by this jini parameter.  
  

### **6.69 TactonIPAddr**

  
Version:v2.3  
Global parameter only  
This parameter is used when you want to run Tacton as a service. In the field paramdata you enter: the path to server manager, the port which the server manager listens to and the name of the server. For example: //localhost:9090/nameOfServer1. If you want to use multiple servers, use comma as separator. For example: //localhost:9090/nameOfServer1,//otherhost:9090/nameOfServer2.  
  
If you do not want to run TCServer as a service, leave the field paramdata empty.  
  

### **6.70 PrinterFormat**

Defines a specific spool file format to be sent to the template editor. Use this parameter if you want to use a spool file format that is different from the standard spool file format used by Windows.  
  
Possible values (file formats):  
 - EMF  
 - RAW  
  
For more info about spool file formats, you can refer to Microsofts documentation regarding Windows printing process on the net.  

### **6.71 ProcessModelerReadOnly**

  
Version:v3.5.1c  
Default value = N  
It is possible to set Jeeves Process Modeler to read-only when starting Process Modeler from Jeeves start menu.  
  
If the parameter is set to Y it is not possible to save changes for the charts in Jeeves Process Modeler.  
  
Supported in Jeeves Process Modeler version 3.0 and above.  
  

### **6.72 ProcessModelerDocumentPath**

It is possible to set Jeeves Process Modeler to use a common path for documents.  
  
If the parameter is set to a path the tag $DOCUMENTPATH$ can be used for file paths in Jeeves Process Modeler to refer to the path in the jini parameter.  
Supported in Jeeves Process Modeler version 3.0 and above.  

### **6.73 JeevesDocumentationUrl**

This parameter is introduced for Jeeves web-based documentation. It is used to specify either the URL for the web-based documentation, or the path to the chm files for the "old" HTML documentation, depending on which version of the documentation is to be used during a transitional period.  
  
The HTML version of the documentation will be replaced by the web-based documentation, which implies that the parameter should always specify the URL for the web-based documentation after being made public.  

### **6.74 UseCDD**

  
Version:3.0  
Default value = Y  
Parameter to specify if the kernel should retrieve data from the CustomerDropDown tables when loading data into the form or list window. This is more for performance, the actual function is activated via an application parameter.  
  

### **6.75 XMLPropsDialog**

If the value is N the XML printer property dialog is not displayed when printing to the XML adapter.  

### **6.76 XMLPrintAllFields**

Specifies whether all visible fields in the template should be printed in the XML file or not. This parameter can only be set for all users.  
  
Y = All visible fields will be printed, irrespective of whether the field has a value or not. This can result in empty tags in the XML file.  
 N = Only visible fields that have a value will be printed in the XML file.  
  
The XML file contains all visible fields in the printed template. If you add a field to the Jeeves template it will appear as a new tag in the XML file as well.  
  
It is important to set this parameter to Y while designing templates in StreamServe. When the design is finished the parameter can be set to N.  

### **6.77 XMLNoNewDocTag**

  
Version:2.3.2  
Default value = N  
From version 2.3.2 a new tag, , was added to the XML file in order to separate documents from each other within the same XML file. This parameter was created to make it possible to remove the  tag from the XML file to support earlier versions.  
  
Y = The  tag will be removed from the XML file  
N = The XML file will contain a  tag (default)  
  

### **6.78 DefaultDateTimeMask**

This parameter is no longer used (as of kernel version 4.0). From this version, the datetime format is set via a dialog opened from Tools, Settings, General... and is stored in the site repository. See the chapter on settings on the Tools menu.  

### **6.79 MaxNoOfClients**

  
Version:350  
Global parameter only  
This parameter determines how many Jeeves clients a user should be allowed to have open simultaneously. If you set Parameter data = 2, a user can start 2 clients but when he/she tries to start a third the client will close down and send out a message stating that max number of concurrent clients has been exceeded.   
  
If "Max no of clients" (maxnoofclients) is set in program "Users in Jeeves" (xsy2) this will apply for that specific user and not the value set in jini parameter MaxNumberOfClients.  
There is no limitation on the number of concurrent clients if there is no value set either in jini or in program "Users in Jeeves" (xsy2).  
  

### **6.80 SaveUserLoginHistory**

  
Version:351  
Default value = 0 only global setting  
If set to 1, a history of clients logged in is saved to table kernel\_usrsessionshistory.   
It can be viewed from an application program with the same name.  
  

### **6.81 EnableSkype**

  
Version:3.0.2  
Default value = N only global setting  
Jeeves' built-in collaboration functionality has been discontinued from kernel 4.0.  
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*  
  
Parameter that defines if skype integration is active when using Jeeves collaboration.  
  

### **6.82 XMLEncoding**

  
Version:3.5.1  
Global parameter only  
This setting makes it possible to change the encoding for the XML files and if not set they are created using the charset from the Jeeves server process.  
  
Possible values are utf-8 and utf-16 where utf-8 is recommended by Streamserve/Addoro.  
  

### **6.83 XMLCharIgnoreList**

Parameter used to specify a list of characters that should be ignored by the XML Adapter when exporting reports to XML. Any character that should not be included in the written XML element data should be specified with its character code as a decimal value. If more than one character is specified the codes should be separated by commas.  
  
With this setting you can guarantee that non-printable characters will not be included in the generated XML element data.  

### **6.84 MinAllowedClientVersion**

If the client version is lower than the value specified by this parameter, it is not allowed to connect. An error message is displayed and the client is automatically closed.  
  
If this parameter does not exist or has the value NULL (default value), there will be no control on the lowest allowed version and any client can connect.  

### **6.85 ReadSiteSettingsOnCompanyChange**

  
Version:  
Default value = N  
Set this parameter to Y if site settings are to be (re)read from the site when changing company (foretagkod) in the client.  
  

7 Menu
------

### **7.1 Hidden**

Hides menu options.   
  
Data section shall have the format [xx,yy,zz] where xx, yy, zz are different menu IDs that you want to hide.   
  
Example:  
Data: [928,929]  
  
The example above hides menu options 928 (Edit terms) and 929 (Edit hidden terms).   

8 Pvm
-----

### **8.1 TabKey**

  
Version:3.0  
Default value = 1  
Used in Product variant nanagement (pvm).  
Controls the use of the Tab key and Enter, when navigating in the PVM matrix.  
  
0= Enter key moves to next cell  
1= Tab key moves to next cell  
  

### **8.2 CellChangeDelay**

  
Version:3.5  
Default value = 2000  
Number of milliseconds after tabbing to a new cell before the cell change event is triggered. An integer greater than 100.

10 SSRS
-------

### **10.1 ReportingServicesURL**

Specifies the URL where the report file is stored on the reporting services server. In the Parameter data field, enter the URL where you have configured the reporting services in the format: [Web Service URL]/ReportExecution2005.asmx.  
  
Example:  
  
http://JVSSTO001:81/ReportServer\_JVSSTO01/ReportExecution2005.asmx?  
  

### **10.2 ReportingServicesDatabase**

Specifies the database in which metadata about reporting services are stored.   
  
If the SSRS report database is not specified in the kernel parameter, then default is JeevesMaster.  
   
 Note that this parameter is not valid for Kernel versions 5.1 R3 and above.  

### **10.3 ReportIdLowerBound**

Specifies the lower boundary value for the report ID (reportid) for SSRS. It is used when storing SSRS reports in the Report Library table (zrep).   
  
This value is also used to distinguish Crystal reports from SSRS reports. You cannot store a Crystal report with an ID equal to or greater than the value specified in this parameter. For example if the parameter value is set to 2010, Crystal reports can be created and successfully executed with the value of a report ID upto 2010.  
  
If no value is not specified, the default value is 20000.  

11 Zero
-------

### **11.1 ShowDebuginfo**

Y means that the title bar in all programs and windows in JEEVES will contain the system designation for the relevant program, relevant program node or relevant window (Window context).

            [3.2 Leverantrsbetalningar via fil, fakturabetalningsservice:](#section3.2)  

            [3.3 Enstaka betalningar/betalningar utan betalningsfiler:](#section3.3)  

            [3.4 Preliminra leverantrsbetalningar:](#section3.4)

  

I Jeeves kan du hantera bank- och postgirobetalningar till leverantrer p tv stt:  
  
- Via fakturabetalningsservice, vilket innebr att du skickar fakturor till en bank, som bevakar dem och betalar dem p frfallodagen.  
  
- Intern bevakning och betalning  
  
I detta kapitel beskriver vi egen bevakning och betalning. Detta tillvgagngsstt innebr att du vanligtvis bevakar dina fakturor sjlv, vljer ut de du vill betala, skapar en bank- eller postgirofil och verfr den fr omedelbar betalning. Fr eventuella fakturor som har passerat sitt frfallodatum ndras frfallodatumet till dagens datum i utbetalningsfilen. Avsikten r att komma frbi problemet nr man inte kan betala fakturor retroaktivt. Slutligen skapar du en bokfringsverifikation, varefter fakturorna ses som betalda i leverantrsreskontran och huvudboken.

Du kan bara skapa filer fr utbetalningsjournaler med status Registrerad, ivgsnd (1) och Klar, betald (5). Den sistnmnda bara s lnge journalen inte r konterad.

### **Utbetalningsjournal** [(Program: xju)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_xju.HTM)

### Skriv ut rapport: **Skapa utbetalningsfil enl utb.vg** [(rJuX2uv)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_rJuX2uv.HTM)

Rapportprogram som skapar utbetalningsfil utifrn selekterad utbetalningsjournal. Filens utseende styrs av angiven utbetalningsvg. Denna hantering r frmst avsedd fr utlandsbetalningar dr utseendet p filen r olika beroende p vilken bank som ska utfra utlandsbetalningen men den kan ocks anvnds fr inhemska utbetalningar om du av ngon anledning vill styra filens skvg och namn per utbetalningsvg.

### **1.4 Skicka fil (externt verfringsprogram)**

Skicka filen till bankgirot eller motsvarande med hjlp av fristende programvara som tillhandahlls av bankerna. Sigillberkning sker ven via dessa program.  

### **1.5 Fyll i datum fr ivgsndning**

### **Utbetalningsjournal** [(Program: xju)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_xju.HTM)

#### Aktuella/viktiga flt/knappar

##### **Snt till bank, datum** [(Flt:: banksanddat)](ms-its:Terms_SE.chm::/ted_banksanddat.HTM)

Datum d utbetalningsfil skapades samt sndes till bank.  
  
 Obs!  
 Det r viktigt att ange ett datum hr. Jeeves kontroller om detta flt r ifyllt. Om det r tomt, r det mjligt att ta bort en utbetalningsjournal, vilket innebr att en ny kan skapas p samma fakturor som drmed blir dubbelbetalda.  
  

### **1.6 Avprickning via fil, importera utbetalningar frn fil**

### **Import extern data->arbetstabell** [(Program: vsthi)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_vsthi.HTM)

Program fr att vlja ut en importdefinition fr att lsa in extern data frn filer in i tabeller i Jeeves databas. Leta upp importdefinitionen i frga och kr rapporten Import -> Conv (rSthiC).   
  
Du skapar de relevanta rapportdefinitionerna i programmet Def och import extern data->arbetstabell (Sthi). Det finns viktig information, som du behver lsa i programhjlpen fr sthi.

### Skriv ut rapport: **Import frn fil** [(rsthic)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_rsthic.HTM)

Program fr inlsning av extern data frn fil till tabell i Jeeves-databasen enligt selekterad importdefinition.  
  
Du sker fram nskad importdefinition innan du krrapportprogrammet. Ngon utskrift grs inte.  
  
Vid inlsning av in-/utbetalningar till arbetstabellen Krin skapas en kvittensjournal som innehller alla inlsta poster samt status p hur inlsningen har gtt. Du kan titta p kvittensjournalen och kontrollera resultatet av inlsningen i programmen Kvittenser inbetalningar (krkh) resp. Kvittenser utbetalningar (lrkh).
Jeeves skapar en kvittensjournal per utbetalningsslag som innehller alla inlsta fakturor frn filen. Utbetalningsslag hmtas frn respektive faktura. Vid inlsningen kontrolleras att leverantren och fakturan finns, att beloppet stmmer och att fakturan inte redan r betald. Varje faktura mrks med aktuell status. Eventuella felaktiga fakturor mste rttas manuellt.  
  
Jeeves kontroller varje faktura vid import, fr att se om den ingr i en utbetalningsjournal med status Klar, skickad. Statusen fr befintliga journaler ndras till Klar, betald, nr alla fakturor i journalen r avprickade vid import, och betalade. Du mste sedan integrera journalen med redovisningen.   
  
Varje fil frn bankgirot innehller endast betalningar som utfrts samma dag.  

### **Kvittenser utbetalningar** [(Program: lrkh)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_lrkh.HTM)

I detta program kan du se resultatet efter import av bankgirofil (leverantrsbetalningar) som krts i programmet Import extern data till arbetstabell (vsthi).  
  
Om en eller flera fakturor gick bra att lsa in, d.v.s. Jeeves hittade en matchande faktura i leverantrsreskontran, fr kvittensjournalen status Utbetalningsjournal skapad och ett utbetalningsjournalnummer. Om ingen faktura kunde importeras fr kvittensjournalen status Skapad.   
  
I den inbddade listan Utbetalningsfiler, kvittens, detaljer framgr statusen p varje enskild faktura. Fakturor som inte har status OK mste regleras manuellt.  
  
Hantering av ofullstndiga betalningar  
 ---------------------------------------------------  
Det finns ett stt att hantera betalningar, importerade frn fil, som visar ofullstndiga transaktioner. P s stt kan du lgga till information sjlv, och drigenom uppn en hgre grad av matchning.  
  
Fr betalningstransaktioner som saknar information, och drfr inte kan prickas av mot en faktura, kan du manuellt lgga integrationskllan (t.ex. Manuell registrering), ett konto och alla andra kontodelar p utbetalningsdetaljerna i den inbddade listan i detta program. Du mste ocks ange status 160, OK med annan integrationsklla, fr att indikera att transaktionen har genomfrts manuellt och r klar fr vidare bearbetning.  
  
Nr du skapar en utbetalningsjournal genom att klicka p knappen Skapa journal i detta program, skapas verifikationer fr dessa manuellt registrerade utbetalningstransaktioner och sparas separat som vnteverifikationer.   
  
Vnteverifikationer kan drefter flyttas till redovisningen p vanligt stt, d.v.s. genom att markera dem som klara och kra flyttrapporten i programmet Mellanlagringsverifikation (xmvt).

Konteringarna i denna verifikation styrs av konteringsreglerna i konteringsmallar fr utbetalningar (program: Xaku eller Aklru).

2 Makulering av felaktig inbetalning
------------------------------------

I Jeeves kan du makulera felaktiga utbetalningar som beskrivs i hjlptexten fr knappen Reversera journal.  

### **Utbetalningsjournal** [(Program: xju)](ms-its:Programs_SE.chm::/pgm_xju.HTM)

### Aktuella funktionsknappar/berknade flt

#### **Reversera journal** [(Knapp/flt: PB\_Reverse\_Xju\_Journal)](ms-its:Terms_SE.chm::/ted_PB_Reverse_Xju_Journal.HTM)

Funktion fr reversering av en betald och bokfrd betalningsjournal. Anvnd funktionen till att reversera alla betalningar i journalen om du av ngon anledning behver terppna en eller flera betalda leverantrsfakturor, till exempel nr pengar betalas tillbaka frn en leverantr.  
  
Nr GENLED085=N reverseras journalen och en ny reverserad journal skapas med verifikationen uppdaterad i redovisningen (status = 8. Saldouppdatering utfrd). Den motbokade verifikationen motkonterar den ursprungliga verifikationen. Leverantrsfakturan terstlls med tidigare status och utestende belopp.  
  
Nr GENLED085=Y reverseras journalen och en ny reverserad journal skapas med status=1 Registrering avslutad. Leverantrsfakturan terstlls med tidigare status och utestende belopp.  
  
Om du stter GENLED085 till Y och gr de ndvndiga instllningarna av valutan och huvudbokskontot, samlar Jeeves in FIFO-saldoposter fr valutan i en srskild tabell (xx\_fifo). Denna tabell tar emot nya saldoposter under integreringen av inkommande betalningar med huvudboken. Detta r anledningen till att den nya reverserade journalen skapas med status=1, Registrering avslutad: att lta anvndaren integrera med huvudboken och p s stt uppdatera tabellen xx\_fifo med nya saldoposter frn de reverserade utestende betalningarna.  
  
Nr journalen reverseras uppdateras tabellen Leverantrsfakturor (lr) med reverseringsdatumet. Datumet visas i fltet Reverserat betalningsdatum (PmtReversalDt) i programmet Leverantrsfakturor (supplinvcs). Det uppdateras ven fr delbetalningar och kan inte ndras manuellt.  
  
 Reversera en enskild leverantrsfaktura  
 -------------------------------------------  
Du kan reversera enskilda fakturor genom att skapa en ny utbetalningsjournal och registrera en negativ utbetalningspost i det hgra fnstret. Du registrerar leverantrsnummer, fakturanummer och ett negativt belopp. Nr du konterar journalen terstlls leverantrsfakturan med tidigare status och utestende belopp.
